coverage: 590 inherited targets in 62 overlapping families plus 26 functional AI targets; open to extension

targets.label: Wakefulness
targets.definition: Wakefulness: waking, becoming drowsy, or falling asleep
targets.candidate_contributors: Accumulating or dissipating sleep pressure; circadian wake signals; activating sensory input; changes in brain function or substance exposure.
targets.conditions: Sleep restriction can impair performance even when reported sleepiness changes little further; felt alertness and measured vigilance can diverge [S01].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Conscious access
targets.definition: Conscious access: an otherwise unreported content entering awareness
targets.candidate_contributors: Making content stronger or longer lasting; removing masking or competing content; directing attention to the relevant feature; connecting input to an available interpretation.
targets.conditions: An accurate response without a report of awareness does not settle conscious access; reporting ability is a separate dependency.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Awareness breadth
targets.definition: Awareness breadth: more or less of an experience being noticed
targets.candidate_contributors: Scanning additional sensory or internal channels; loosening a narrow task focus; reducing a dominant competing demand; supplying prompts for previously omitted aspects.
targets.conditions: Noticing more aspects can reduce detail per aspect. Attention breadth and experienced awareness are related but distinct targets.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Clarity
targets.definition: Clarity: experience becoming clearer, hazier, or more confused
targets.candidate_contributors: Resolving conflicting interpretations; restoring missing context; improving signal quality; reducing simultaneous demands; changes in physiological alertness.
targets.conditions: Identify whether the haze concerns sensory input, meaning, memory, or wakefulness; the same intervention need not affect each.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Absorption
targets.definition: Absorption: becoming immersed in, or disengaging from, an activity
targets.candidate_contributors: A continuously available task; successive challenges within current capability; compelling sensory or narrative continuity; reduced interruptions; stronger competing events that break immersion.
targets.conditions: Immersion can support an activity or conceal relevant surroundings. Its value depends on what requires access.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Dream awareness
targets.definition: Dream awareness: recognizing a dream while dreaming
targets.candidate_contributors: A dream containing a noticed inconsistency; recall of an intention to recognize dreaming; emergence of reflective awareness during sleep.
targets.conditions: These are candidate relationships, not a reliable induction method; remembering a dream later does not establish awareness during it.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Self-awareness
targets.definition: Self-awareness: noticing oneself as participating in an experience
targets.candidate_contributors: A prompt to notice one's current action; reflection or self-reference; attention to one's bodily participation; feedback showing one's contribution to an event.
targets.conditions: Self-monitoring may become distraction or evaluative self-consciousness; noticing oneself need not improve performance.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Environmental awareness
targets.definition: Environmental awareness: becoming more or less aware of surroundings
targets.candidate_contributors: Unobstructed sensory access; scanning the surroundings; cues identifying consequential changes; releasing attention from an absorbing internal or external task.
targets.conditions: Information must actually reach the person; a warning cannot reveal an inaccessible environment by itself.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Fatigue
targets.definition: Fatigue: feeling more or less mentally or physically tired
targets.candidate_contributors: Accumulated exertion and sleep loss; relief from sustained demands; illness-related bodily signals; changes in perceived remaining effort and payoff.
targets.conditions: Felt fatigue, physical exhaustion, and declining accuracy require separate interpretation; their trajectories may differ [S01].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Vitality
targets.definition: Vitality: feeling more or less energetic or vigorous
targets.candidate_contributors: Recovery from depletion; activating movement or sensory experience; anticipated achievable reward; relief from sustained stress or obstructed effort.
targets.conditions: An energizing interpretation cannot be assumed to correct a physiological limitation; vitality is a felt outcome.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Comfort
targets.definition: Comfort: changes in felt ease, discomfort, or restlessness
targets.candidate_contributors: Changing pressure, posture, temperature, noise, or bodily irritation; meeting an unmet bodily need; increasing predictability and control over the setting.
targets.conditions: The contributor depends on the source of discomfort; social reassurance cannot remove an uncomfortable physical stimulus.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Pain
targets.definition: Pain: changes in experienced intensity, location, unpleasantness, or meaning
targets.candidate_contributors: Changes in nociceptive input or central processing; attention to pain; expected relief or threat; the meaning assigned to the sensation.
targets.conditions: Intensity, unpleasantness, and interpretation can change separately. Expectation effects in experimental pain do not establish removal of injury [S02].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Tension
targets.definition: Tension: changes in felt tightness, relaxation, or readiness
targets.candidate_contributors: Changes in muscle contraction and posture; preparing for or ending an anticipated action; perceived threat; deliberate release of a held contraction.
targets.conditions: Felt tightness may persist without voluntary contraction; a bodily description alone does not identify its cause.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Hunger and satiety
targets.definition: Hunger and satiety: changes in felt need for or satisfaction from food
targets.candidate_contributors: Signals of energy need; oral and gastrointestinal input from eating; learned meal cues; anticipated food; sensory-specific loss of appeal during consumption.
targets.conditions: Wanting a particular food and general hunger can diverge; the relevant contributor depends on which is changing.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Thirst
targets.definition: Thirst: changes in felt need for fluid
targets.candidate_contributors: Body-fluid regulation; dry-mouth sensations; oral signals from drinking; heat and fluid loss; learned access cues.
targets.conditions: Dry mouth and physiological fluid need are not interchangeable; this is a contributor map, not intake guidance.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Sexual arousal
targets.definition: Sexual arousal: changes in felt sexual responsiveness or interest
targets.candidate_contributors: Personally meaningful erotic cues or imagination; wanted touch and interaction; bodily and hormonal state; relationship context; stress or distraction.
targets.conditions: Subjective desire, physiological response, willingness, and consent are separate; none can be inferred solely from another.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Bodily orientation
targets.definition: Bodily orientation: changes in felt balance, movement, position, or ownership
targets.candidate_contributors: Vestibular, visual, and proprioceptive input; actual movement; agreement or conflict between seen and felt position; expected sensory consequences of action.
targets.conditions: Balance, location, movement, and ownership can dissociate; specify the component before selecting a contributor.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Interoceptive awareness
targets.definition: Interoceptive awareness: changes in noticing and distinguishing internal bodily signals
targets.candidate_contributors: Directing attention to internal signals; distinguishing similar sensations; labeling location and quality; comparing sensations with independently available physiological information.
targets.conditions: Greater confidence in bodily interpretation need not mean greater accuracy; indiscriminate monitoring may amplify ambiguity.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Alertness
targets.definition: Alertness: becoming more or less ready to detect events
targets.candidate_contributors: A temporally informative warning; an imminent detection requirement; changing sleep pressure; activating or monotonous input.
targets.conditions: Brief alerting and sustained vigilance differ; temporary stimulation does not establish restored performance after sleep loss [S01].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Agitation
targets.definition: Agitation: becoming more or less unsettled or activated
targets.candidate_contributors: Unexpected demands; unresolved threat or conflict; intense stimulation; physiological activation; removal of the provoking condition.
targets.conditions: Quiet behavior may conceal continuing agitation; reducing expression alone need not settle the underlying state.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Composure
targets.definition: Composure: gaining or losing the ability to remain settled under pressure
targets.candidate_contributors: A practiced response available under pressure; predictable next steps; perceived control over a consequential action; recovery time; reinterpretation of the demand.
targets.conditions: Composure can coexist with strong emotion; a calm-sounding instruction is not evidence that composure occurred.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Vigilance
targets.definition: Vigilance: changing readiness to detect possible threats or opportunities
targets.candidate_contributors: Expected event frequency and consequence; learned warning cues; instructions specifying what to monitor; recent alarms or misses.
targets.conditions: Excessive monitoring can increase false alarms and consume attention needed elsewhere; specify the relevant threat or opportunity.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Startle readiness
targets.definition: Startle readiness: changing susceptibility to sudden interruption
targets.candidate_contributors: Sudden stimulus intensity; uncertainty about onset; prior warning; current defensive activation; repetition that changes the event's novelty.
targets.conditions: Preparation for a known event and general sensitization can move startle differently.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Felt safety
targets.definition: Felt safety: a situation coming to feel safer or more threatening
targets.candidate_contributors: Removal of an actual threat; credible protection or escape options; trustworthy responses from others; new evidence about a previously ambiguous situation.
targets.conditions: Felt safety can be inaccurate. Reassurance without changed grounds may alter feeling while leaving danger unchanged.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Action readiness
targets.definition: Action readiness: becoming poised for approach, withdrawal, speech, or movement
targets.candidate_contributors: A recognized opportunity or threat; a selected response; motor preparation; availability of the required object or opening; learned action cues.
targets.conditions: Readiness is specific to an action; general activation can leave the needed response unavailable.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Recovery
targets.definition: Recovery: returning more quickly or slowly after activation
targets.candidate_contributors: Termination of the provoking input; recognition that the episode has ended; disengagement from repeated threat simulation; restoration of bodily resources.
targets.conditions: Returning to baseline and recovering usable capability are distinct; continuing demands can repeatedly restart activation.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Detection
targets.definition: Detection: becoming able or unable to notice a stimulus
targets.candidate_contributors: Greater signal intensity or duration; reduced masking; informative timing or location cues; a response criterion more willing to report a signal.
targets.conditions: More detections may come from more false alarms rather than improved sensitivity.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Sensitivity
targets.definition: Sensitivity: weaker or stronger stimulation becoming noticeable
targets.candidate_contributors: Changes in sensory adaptation; lower background noise; attention to the relevant channel; physiological sensory function.
targets.conditions: Distinguish a changed threshold from changed willingness to report and from an altered physical stimulus.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Resolution
targets.definition: Resolution: distinguishing finer or coarser sensory differences
targets.candidate_contributors: Access to fine features; side-by-side contrasts; repeated discrimination of near neighbors; informative correction about the confusable feature.
targets.conditions: Improvement may remain specific to the practiced stimulus, position, or task [S03].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Auditory discrimination
targets.definition: Auditory discrimination: distinguishing sounds, voices, tones, or rhythms
targets.candidate_contributors: Contrasting confusable sounds; isolating pitch, timing, or timbre differences; reduced acoustic masking; pairing a sound with its correct source or label.
targets.conditions: Volume alone cannot teach a phonetic distinction; auditory access and learned discrimination impose different limits.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Visual discrimination
targets.definition: Visual discrimination: distinguishing shapes, colors, movements, or configurations
targets.candidate_contributors: Comparing confusable shapes or configurations; highlighting diagnostic visual features; repeated discrimination; improved contrast or visibility.
targets.conditions: Texture-learning results support local learning, not a general improvement in all vision [S03].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Tactile discrimination
targets.definition: Tactile discrimination: distinguishing textures, pressures, or locations
targets.candidate_contributors: Controlled differences in texture or pressure; exploring an object through movement; contrast between nearby locations; feedback identifying the relevant sensation.
targets.conditions: Skin location, stimulus force, and sensory function constrain which distinctions become available.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Smell and taste discrimination
targets.definition: Smell and taste discrimination: distinguishing previously conflated sensations
targets.candidate_contributors: Comparing samples while tracking a specific sensory dimension; identifying component qualities; reduced competing odors or tastes; changes in adaptation.
targets.conditions: A richer label vocabulary can change reports without establishing finer sensory sensitivity.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Signal discrimination
targets.definition: Signal discrimination: separating a relevant signal from background variation
targets.candidate_contributors: Reducing irrelevant variation; revealing a diagnostic feature; comparing signal-present and signal-absent cases; calibrating the reporting criterion.
targets.conditions: Signal quality and decision bias need separate checks; added salience can amplify noise as well as signal.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Figure and ground
targets.definition: Figure and ground: changing which part stands out against a background
targets.candidate_contributors: Contrast in color, motion, depth, or contour; directing attention to a region; changing which shape is treated as the foreground.
targets.conditions: A foreground shift changes organization without requiring a change in the physical objects.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Grouping
targets.definition: Grouping: experiencing separate elements as a unit or a unit as separate
targets.candidate_contributors: Proximity, similarity, continuity, or shared movement; common labels; enclosing boundaries; a task that treats elements jointly.
targets.conditions: Perceptual unity does not establish that the elements form a causal or functional unit.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Boundary perception
targets.definition: Boundary perception: changing where one perceived thing ends and another begins
targets.candidate_contributors: Sharper edges; occlusion cues; discontinuities in color, motion, or texture; explicit segmentation; alternative object interpretations.
targets.conditions: A drawn border can impose a division that the underlying process does not have.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Ambiguity resolution
targets.definition: Ambiguity resolution: moving between interpretations of an ambiguous stimulus
targets.candidate_contributors: Context favoring one interpretation; cues diagnostic between alternatives; prior exposure; attention to an interpretation-specific feature.
targets.conditions: An interpretation becoming dominant does not prove it uniquely fits an ambiguous stimulus.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Spatial organization
targets.definition: Spatial organization: changing perceived depth, distance, orientation, or layout
targets.candidate_contributors: Changing viewpoint; movement-based depth information; binocular and perspective cues; landmarks; explicit orientation information.
targets.conditions: A map can improve layout knowledge without changing every immediate depth percept.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Temporal organization
targets.definition: Temporal organization: experiencing events as simultaneous, sequential, or rhythmic
targets.candidate_contributors: Event spacing; repeated rhythm; onset cues; grouping events into units; expectations about sequence.
targets.conditions: Perceived simultaneity and physical simultaneity differ; retrospective grouping may change the experienced sequence.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Multisensory integration
targets.definition: Multisensory integration: changing how signals from different senses are combined
targets.candidate_contributors: Cross-sensory agreement in timing and location; reliability of each channel; compatible or conflicting source cues.
targets.conditions: Visual speech can alter what is heard [S04]; integration can introduce error when signals have different sources.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Perceptual constancy
targets.definition: Perceptual constancy: changing what is treated as stable despite changing input
targets.candidate_contributors: Stable relationships across viewpoints; information about illumination, distance, or movement; comparison with a reference object.
targets.conditions: Constancy is inferred across changing input; unusual contexts can make a normally useful inference misleading.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Identity recognition
targets.definition: Identity recognition: recognizing a person, object, place, or event
targets.candidate_contributors: Diagnostic identifying features; exposure to different views of the same entity; retrieval cues; distinguishing the entity from similar alternatives.
targets.conditions: Familiarity can occur without correct identity; resemblance is insufficient when impostors or duplicates are possible.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Pattern recognition
targets.definition: Pattern recognition: noticing a repeated or governing arrangement
targets.candidate_contributors: Juxtaposing instances; aligning repeated relations; removing irrelevant surface differences; representing the arrangement explicitly.
targets.conditions: A visible regularity may be accidental; recognizing it and establishing its reliability are separate changes.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Familiarity
targets.definition: Familiarity: something coming to feel familiar or unfamiliar
targets.candidate_contributors: Prior encounters; repeated exposure; overlap with known features; easier processing; contextual reminders.
targets.conditions: Familiarity is not evidence of truth, safety, prior agreement, or accurate recollection.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Application recognition
targets.definition: Application recognition: recognizing that a known method applies here
targets.candidate_contributors: Matching current preconditions to a known method; contrasting an applicable and inapplicable case; indexing the method by the situation it resolves.
targets.conditions: A shared topic is insufficient; the method's required inputs and exclusions must fit.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Opportunity recognition
targets.definition: Opportunity recognition: noticing an available beneficial possibility
targets.candidate_contributors: Making an unused resource or opening visible; connecting it to a valued consequence; removing an assumed constraint; identifying a feasible next move.
targets.conditions: An attractive imaginable outcome becomes an opportunity only if some route is available under the actual conditions.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Hazard recognition
targets.definition: Hazard recognition: noticing a consequential threat or failure possibility
targets.candidate_contributors: Diagnostic warning signs; causal knowledge of a failure path; comparison with a near miss; visibility of consequential dependencies.
targets.conditions: Vivid examples can inflate perceived prevalence; detection of possibility and estimation of likelihood are different.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Incongruity recognition
targets.definition: Incongruity recognition: noticing that elements do not fit together
targets.candidate_contributors: Making incompatible elements simultaneously available; stating the expected relation; comparing the case with that relation.
targets.conditions: An apparent mismatch can arise from a mistaken expectation rather than from a defective case.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Affordance recognition
targets.definition: Affordance recognition: noticing what an object or situation permits one to do
targets.candidate_contributors: Visible handles, openings, and controls; demonstrations of use; knowledge of object properties; fit between bodily capability and environment.
targets.conditions: What an object permits depends on the actor; an apparent affordance may be inaccessible or deceptive.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Orientation
targets.definition: Orientation: directing attention toward something previously unattended
targets.candidate_contributors: A spatial or verbal cue; sudden change; a question naming an overlooked feature; an object connected to the active goal.
targets.conditions: Orienting toward something consumes attention elsewhere; the selected direction must serve the current activity.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Selection
targets.definition: Selection: changing which competing content receives attention
targets.candidate_contributors: A current selection rule; relative salience; reward history; removing distractors; placing needed content at the decision point.
targets.conditions: Selecting more relevant content can improve use of limited memory; selection efficiency is not identical to memory capacity [S05].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Maintenance
targets.definition: Maintenance: sustaining attention for a longer or shorter interval
targets.candidate_contributors: A continuously meaningful task signal; manageable substeps; reminders of the active object; reduced interruptions; planned points for reorientation.
targets.conditions: Persistence without sensitivity to changed conditions can become fixation.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Disengagement
targets.definition: Disengagement: releasing attention from a currently dominant object
targets.candidate_contributors: A clear completion or suspension condition; recording the unfinished matter; a stronger relevant cue; reducing repeated re-exposure.
targets.conditions: Disengagement can leave unresolved work unavailable later unless a return condition is preserved.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Switching
targets.definition: Switching: moving attention between objects or activities
targets.candidate_contributors: An explicit switch cue; visible state of the incoming task; preservation of the outgoing task's state; removal of obsolete instructions.
targets.conditions: A fast switch can still carry the previous rule into the new task.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Division
targets.definition: Division: distributing attention across multiple demands
targets.candidate_contributors: Separating demands by timing or modality; automating a practiced component; external monitoring of one stream; explicit priority when demands conflict.
targets.conditions: Several demanding operations may still compete for the same capacity; division is not unlimited parallel processing.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Breadth
targets.definition: Breadth: narrowing focus or taking in a wider field
targets.candidate_contributors: A prompt to inspect context or detail; changing display scale; reducing a dominant threat cue; making peripheral information relevant.
targets.conditions: Widening attention can sacrifice precision; narrowing can hide a consequential dependency.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Interruption resistance
targets.definition: Interruption resistance: becoming more or less distractible
targets.candidate_contributors: Removing avoidable alerts; distinguishing interruption criteria; making the active goal continuously available; arranging a protected work interval.
targets.conditions: Necessary warnings still need an access route; complete isolation can obstruct required information.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Timing
targets.definition: Timing: attending at the moment a relevant difference occurs
targets.candidate_contributors: A cue synchronized with the event; predictable intervals; a reminder at the point of use; maintaining the relevant detection rule.
targets.conditions: Information delivered too early may be forgotten and too late may be unusable.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Control
targets.definition: Control: changing the relation between chosen and involuntary attention
targets.candidate_contributors: A deliberately chosen focus; recognition of capture; an available return action; environmental control over recurring distractors.
targets.conditions: Voluntary instructions compete with learned and stimulus-driven capture; wanting control does not establish it.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Noticeability
targets.definition: Noticeability: something becoming harder or easier to overlook
targets.candidate_contributors: Contrast, placement, repetition, labeling, novelty, or a distinctive comparison; removing competing emphasis.
targets.conditions: If everything is highlighted, the intended item may gain no relative noticeability.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Importance
targets.definition: Importance: changing how much something seems to matter
targets.candidate_contributors: Showing consequences for a valued concern; changing the scale or scope represented; making a neglected dependency visible.
targets.conditions: Something can feel important because it is vivid even when its consequence is small.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Urgency
targets.definition: Urgency: changing how soon something seems to require a response
targets.candidate_contributors: A real deadline; showing how delay changes options; detecting an approaching threshold; distinguishing reversible from expiring opportunities.
targets.conditions: Urgency should change with delay cost; artificial pressure can produce haste without improving the choice.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Personal relevance
targets.definition: Personal relevance: connecting or disconnecting a matter from oneself
targets.candidate_contributors: Connecting the matter to an actual goal, experience, role, relationship, or constraint; supplying a self-relevant example.
targets.conditions: Invented personalization can make an inaccurate connection feel intimate; use available recipient context.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Practical relevance
targets.definition: Practical relevance: seeing or losing a connection to an actual activity
targets.candidate_contributors: Showing where the information enters a real operation; supplying a needed input; demonstrating a changed decision or action.
targets.conditions: An abstract statement of usefulness leaves practical relevance unspecified.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Emotional prominence
targets.definition: Emotional prominence: an item occupying more or less affective attention
targets.candidate_contributors: An emotionally charged association; a concrete consequence for someone valued; repeated affective attention; reinterpreting the event's significance.
targets.conditions: Emotional prominence can increase without improved understanding or warranted priority.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Backgrounding
targets.definition: Backgrounding: an acknowledged matter ceasing to dominate
targets.candidate_contributors: Resolving the concern; recording it with a return trigger; changing its perceived relevance; reducing repeated cues that reactivate it.
targets.conditions: Backgrounding can be useful even while the matter remains unresolved, provided later access is preserved.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Priority competition
targets.definition: Priority competition: changing which of several concerns comes to the foreground
targets.candidate_contributors: Explicit precedence between concerns; visibility of opportunity costs; current consequences; deadlines; removing irrelevant competition.
targets.conditions: The most activating concern need not be the most consequential one.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Entry
targets.definition: Entry: making a representation available for immediate mental use
targets.candidate_contributors: Presenting the needed content immediately before use; retrieving it with a distinctive cue; translating it into an accessible form.
targets.conditions: Availability requires comprehension and attention; physical presence on a page alone is insufficient.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Maintenance
targets.definition: Maintenance: keeping a representation available during another operation
targets.candidate_contributors: Rehearsing the relevant content; maintaining a visible reference; protecting it from competing input; organizing it into meaningful units.
targets.conditions: External support changes supported performance; it does not by itself expand unaided capacity.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Updating
targets.definition: Updating: replacing outdated active content with current content
targets.candidate_contributors: An authoritative replacement value; an explicit supersession signal; comparison of old and current versions; removal of stale copies.
targets.conditions: Without item identity, replacing a value can update the wrong object.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Binding
targets.definition: Binding: keeping the correct features attached to the correct item
targets.candidate_contributors: Stable names and locations; explicit feature-to-item links; integrated displays; rehearsing the relation as well as each feature.
targets.conditions: Remembering all features separately does not preserve which belongs to which.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Ordering
targets.definition: Ordering: changing the sequence in which active items are represented
targets.candidate_contributors: Numbering; spatial arrangement; a temporal or causal sequence; rehearsing transitions between adjacent elements.
targets.conditions: A memorable order can still be the wrong execution order.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Chunking
targets.definition: Chunking: treating multiple elements as one usable unit
targets.candidate_contributors: A learned pattern that encodes several elements jointly; a meaningful shared structure; a familiar abbreviation with recoverable contents.
targets.conditions: A novel acronym may add another item instead of reducing load; the grouping must already be usable.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Interference
targets.definition: Interference: changing how much one active item disrupts another
targets.candidate_contributors: Reducing similarity between competing items; separating contexts or times; removing irrelevant content; distinctive item labels.
targets.conditions: Interference reduction is different from proving general capacity growth [S05].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Comparison access
targets.definition: Comparison access: making relevant items available together
targets.candidate_contributors: Juxtaposing the relevant items; aligning corresponding dimensions; preserving common units and scope; externalizing one item while using another.
targets.conditions: Two values are not comparable merely because they are adjacent; their meanings must align.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Release
targets.definition: Release: removing no-longer-needed content from active use
targets.candidate_contributors: A completion marker; an explicit discard or defer decision; storing what must survive; removing obsolete prompts.
targets.conditions: Premature release creates omissions if a downstream operation still needs the content.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Recall
targets.definition: Recall: recovering previously unavailable information or experience
targets.candidate_contributors: A distinctive cue; reinstating relevant context; reconstructing associations; narrowing retrieval by time, place, or relation.
targets.conditions: A plausible reconstruction may feel like recall; access and accuracy need separate treatment.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Recognition memory
targets.definition: Recognition memory: identifying something as previously encountered
targets.candidate_contributors: Re-exposure to the item; comparison with remembered features; contextual corroboration; discrimination from similar alternatives.
targets.conditions: Ease or familiarity can produce false recognition without recollection of the encounter.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Cue dependence
targets.definition: Cue dependence: changing which prompts make a memory accessible
targets.candidate_contributors: Encoding with a later-use cue; retrieving the same content from varied prompts; making the cue-content relation distinctive.
targets.conditions: A cue can help only if it connects to a retained representation or supports a valid reconstruction.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Spontaneous retrieval
targets.definition: Spontaneous retrieval: a memory becoming available without deliberate search
targets.candidate_contributors: An environmental reminder; associative overlap with current experience; an unresolved concern; emotional or sensory resemblance.
targets.conditions: Spontaneous arrival does not reveal whether the remembered content is relevant or accurate.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Prospective remembering
targets.definition: Prospective remembering: remembering an intended action when it becomes relevant
targets.candidate_contributors: Linking a specific future event to an action; a visible reminder at that event; rehearsing the event-action pairing.
targets.conditions: The event must be detected and the action feasible; a cue-linked plan is not a substitute for ability [S15].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Source retrieval
targets.definition: Source retrieval: recalling where a representation came from
targets.candidate_contributors: Recording who, where, and when alongside content; source-distinctive cues; comparing the account with the original record.
targets.conditions: A content memory can survive while source information is lost; confident attribution can still be mistaken.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Context retrieval
targets.definition: Context retrieval: recovering the circumstances needed to interpret a memory
targets.candidate_contributors: Restoring original circumstances, definitions, purpose, and constraints; a linked contextual record; cues from the surrounding episode.
targets.conditions: Recovered context must fit this version of the memory rather than a similar encounter.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Relevance retrieval
targets.definition: Relevance retrieval: recovering a memory in a situation where it matters
targets.candidate_contributors: Indexing prior knowledge by its application conditions; comparing the current case with an earlier relational structure; a point-of-use retrieval cue.
targets.conditions: Surface similarity may retrieve the wrong precedent; consequential conditions must match.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Retrieval competition
targets.definition: Retrieval competition: changing which memory comes to mind first
targets.candidate_contributors: Cue specificity; recent retrieval of one candidate; distinctive context labels; separating commonly confused memories.
targets.conditions: Making one memory easier to retrieve can leave equally relevant alternatives less available.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Encoding
targets.definition: Encoding: forming a new memory of an encounter
targets.candidate_contributors: Attention to diagnostic features; relating material to existing knowledge; meaningful organization; active reconstruction during the encounter.
targets.conditions: Exposure alone need not encode the relation later needed; meaningful elaboration can also introduce assumptions.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Retention
targets.definition: Retention: changing how long something remains available
targets.candidate_contributors: Retrieval across later occasions; spacing encounters; preserving usable cues; reduced destructive interference; conditions supporting consolidation.
targets.conditions: Retrieval and restudy can differ by delay: immediate fluency can favor a method that retains less later [S06].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Detail
targets.definition: Detail: retaining, recovering, or losing specific features
targets.candidate_contributors: Attention to exact features; accurate external records; discrimination of similar episodes; retrieval that checks specifics rather than only gist.
targets.conditions: Repeated retelling can stabilize selected details while losing others.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Gist
targets.definition: Gist: retaining or revising the broader meaning of an event
targets.candidate_contributors: Extracting a common relation; summarizing consequences; integrating an event with prior schemas; later reinterpretation.
targets.conditions: A coherent gist can omit an exception that changes the event's meaning.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Association
targets.definition: Association: linking or unlinking memories with other material
targets.candidate_contributors: Repeated co-occurrence; meaningful relational links; contrast with previously associated material; retrieval in a different context.
targets.conditions: Co-occurrence can strengthen an association without showing a causal relationship.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Updating
targets.definition: Updating: incorporating later information into a remembered account
targets.candidate_contributors: New event information; explicit correction of an earlier account; integration with a retained record; identification of what changed.
targets.conditions: Later information can contaminate memory for the original event rather than merely supplement it [S07].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Forgetting
targets.definition: Forgetting: losing access to or retention of prior material
targets.candidate_contributors: Loss of retrieval cues; competing similar material; disuse or disrupted consolidation; changes in neurological function.
targets.conditions: Failure to retrieve does not establish erasure; deliberately withholding use cannot guarantee permanent forgetting.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Source confusion
targets.definition: Source confusion: changing whether an idea is remembered as observed, inferred, or imagined
targets.candidate_contributors: Separating observation, inference, suggestion, and imagination when recording; preserving original wording and provenance; checking later additions.
targets.conditions: Repeated suggestion can alter later reports; labels help only if retained and trusted appropriately [S07].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Accuracy
targets.definition: Accuracy: correcting a memory or introducing a distortion
targets.candidate_contributors: Comparison with contemporaneous evidence; correction of a specific discrepancy; maintaining source boundaries; misleading post-event wording that introduces distortion.
targets.conditions: Agreement among repeated retellings is not independent confirmation [S07].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Emotional association
targets.definition: Emotional association: changing the feeling associated with remembered material
targets.candidate_contributors: New experiences linked to the remembered material; revising its current significance; encountering it in a different emotional context.
targets.conditions: Changed feeling does not rewrite the historical event; durable change cannot be inferred from one retelling.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Concept acquisition
targets.definition: Concept acquisition: gaining a previously unavailable distinction
targets.candidate_contributors: Contrasting cases that require different treatment; diagnostic features; a stable label; using the distinction in classification.
targets.conditions: Labels aided learning in a specific category task [S08]; a word alone does not supply every needed distinction.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Category splitting
targets.definition: Category splitting: separating cases previously treated as equivalent
targets.candidate_contributors: A consequential difference within a class; contrasting outcomes or requirements; explicit subcategory criteria; borderline examples.
targets.conditions: Splitting adds value only if the new boundary supports a needed distinction or operation.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Category merging
targets.definition: Category merging: recognizing cases as belonging to one class
targets.candidate_contributors: A shared governing relation; abstraction from irrelevant differences; a common rule that handles formerly separate cases.
targets.conditions: Merging can destroy exceptions that remain consequential.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Boundary revision
targets.definition: Boundary revision: changing which cases count as members
targets.candidate_contributors: Near-boundary cases; a changed membership criterion; counterexamples; clarification of necessary versus typical features.
targets.conditions: Changing a boundary may change the concept, not merely correct its application.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Prototype revision
targets.definition: Prototype revision: changing what counts as a typical example
targets.candidate_contributors: Exposure to a different distribution of examples; emphasizing previously underrepresented members; comparing a stereotype with actual variation.
targets.conditions: A salient unusual example can distort typicality rather than improve it.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Definition revision
targets.definition: Definition revision: changing what a term or concept commits one to
targets.candidate_contributors: Explicit entailments; ambiguous uses; counterexamples to the current definition; a purpose requiring different commitments.
targets.conditions: A stipulated revision does not retroactively change what previous speakers meant.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Hierarchy revision
targets.definition: Hierarchy revision: changing relations among broader and narrower categories
targets.candidate_contributors: Set inclusion or exclusion relationships; shared and distinguishing properties; cases revealing multiple parent categories.
targets.conditions: A convenient tree can conceal overlapping membership or independent dimensions.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Exception recognition
targets.definition: Exception recognition: identifying limits to an apparent rule
targets.candidate_contributors: A contrary case; a violated precondition; a scope contrast; examination of the supposed rule's quantifier.
targets.conditions: One exception defeats a universal claim but may leave a probabilistic tendency intact.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Concept removal
targets.definition: Concept removal: ceasing to organize a matter through an unhelpful category
targets.candidate_contributors: Showing the category's misleading consequences; replacing its work with more discriminating dimensions; removing habitual labels from the task.
targets.conditions: Deleting a word without replacing its useful distinctions can reduce capability.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Concept transfer
targets.definition: Concept transfer: making a distinction usable in a different domain
targets.candidate_contributors: Aligning relational structure across domains; identifying corresponding roles; constructing a new-domain example and a nonexample.
targets.conditions: Transfer needs shared operative relations, not resemblance of vocabulary [S09].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Verbal representation
targets.definition: Verbal representation: expressing a matter in usable words
targets.candidate_contributors: Naming entities and relations; constructing a concrete sentence; resolving ambiguous referents; supplying words for the missing distinction.
targets.conditions: Fluent wording can conceal unresolved content; verbal availability is not evidence of truth.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Visual representation
targets.definition: Visual representation: making an image or diagram available
targets.candidate_contributors: A diagram or image with meaningful correspondence; contrastive visual examples; spatially displaying otherwise hidden relations.
targets.conditions: Visual detail can imply unsupported precision or causal links; correspondence must remain inspectable.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Spatial representation
targets.definition: Spatial representation: organizing material through positions or distances
targets.candidate_contributors: Assigning stable locations; mapping distance or adjacency to a specified relationship; arranging objects to expose comparisons.
targets.conditions: Spatial distance must mean something defined; arbitrary placement can suggest a false relation.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Quantitative representation
targets.definition: Quantitative representation: expressing magnitudes and relationships numerically
targets.candidate_contributors: Measurement; explicit units and denominators; counting comparable cases; representing uncertainty or scale numerically.
targets.conditions: Numbers without justified measurement rules create precision without a valid quantity.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Procedural representation
targets.definition: Procedural representation: organizing material as something to do
targets.candidate_contributors: Identifying inputs, operations, order, and completion conditions; a worked execution; a branch for a consequential alternative.
targets.conditions: A procedure is usable only when the actor can perform its steps with available inputs.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Narrative representation
targets.definition: Narrative representation: organizing events through a story
targets.candidate_contributors: Temporal order; agents and aims; causally connected events; selecting a viewpoint and relevant turning points.
targets.conditions: Narrative coherence can invite causal conclusions beyond the evidence.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Structural representation
targets.definition: Structural representation: exposing parts, relations, and dependencies
targets.candidate_contributors: Making components and dependencies explicit; distinguishing levels; tracing what consumes each intermediate result.
targets.conditions: A diagram of boxes does not establish the proposed dependencies or their sufficiency.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Compression
targets.definition: Compression: reducing representational size while preserving needed distinctions
targets.candidate_contributors: Removing repetition; substituting known chunks; preserving decision-relevant differences; deleting details irrelevant to the intended use.
targets.conditions: Compression must specify its consumer; lossless for one use can be destructive for another.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Expansion
targets.definition: Expansion: making previously compressed distinctions explicit
targets.candidate_contributors: Unpacking an abbreviation; restoring omitted premises or cases; expanding a formula into operations; exposing hidden choices.
targets.conditions: Expansion helps when it supplies missing distinctions; extra wording can increase load without doing so.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Externalization
targets.definition: Externalization: using an external representation to alter what is mentally available
targets.candidate_contributors: Writing, diagramming, arranging, or computing a representation that can be consulted and manipulated.
targets.conditions: The person must interpret and coordinate with the aid; external form can change task difficulty [S10].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Vocabulary acquisition
targets.definition: Vocabulary acquisition: gaining a word for an available or new distinction
targets.candidate_contributors: Pairing a word with clear examples and counterexamples; retrieval during actual use; correction of a mistaken sense.
targets.conditions: Recognizing the word and producing it appropriately are separate abilities.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Sense selection
targets.definition: Sense selection: changing which meaning of an expression is active
targets.candidate_contributors: Surrounding sentence context; task purpose; speaker usage; a contrast between candidate meanings.
targets.conditions: The locally natural sense may differ from the author's intended technical sense.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Disambiguation
targets.definition: Disambiguation: separating interpretations that had been conflated
targets.candidate_contributors: Enumerating consequential interpretations; a separating example; explicit qualification; replacement of an ambiguous term.
targets.conditions: A preferred reading does not eliminate another reading still permitted by the expression.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Reference resolution
targets.definition: Reference resolution: identifying what a word or statement refers to
targets.candidate_contributors: Shared context; pointing or naming; unique descriptions; resolution of pronoun and scope dependencies.
targets.conditions: A referent must be uniquely recoverable enough for the current use; assumed shared knowledge can fail.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Implication recognition
targets.definition: Implication recognition: noticing what an utterance suggests beyond its literal wording
targets.candidate_contributors: Comparison of literal content with the speaker's situation and purpose; conversational context; plausible alternatives to the chosen wording.
targets.conditions: Implied meaning is defeasible; inference about intent requires more than linguistic plausibility.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Presupposition recognition
targets.definition: Presupposition recognition: noticing what an utterance takes for granted
targets.candidate_contributors: Making the assumed background explicit; considering denial or alternative cases; asking what must already hold for the utterance to function.
targets.conditions: Recognizing a presupposition does not establish that the speaker consciously endorsed it.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Pragmatic interpretation
targets.definition: Pragmatic interpretation: changing the understood purpose of an utterance
targets.candidate_contributors: The interaction's purpose; preceding moves; relationship and setting; recipient response; explicit clarification of intended use.
targets.conditions: Identical words can request, warn, joke, or describe; wording alone may underdetermine the act [S18].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Translation
targets.definition: Translation: making meaning available across languages or vocabularies
targets.candidate_contributors: A correspondence between concepts; contextual examples; disambiguation before substitution; reconstruction of idiom and pragmatic role.
targets.conditions: Word-for-word replacement can preserve terms while changing meaning or interpersonal effect.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Literal and figurative interpretation
targets.definition: Literal and figurative interpretation: changing the role assigned to an expression
targets.candidate_contributors: Genre and context cues; incompatibility of literal reading; a supported metaphorical mapping; explicit literal clarification.
targets.conditions: A vivid analogy may import properties outside the intended mapping.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Expressive precision
targets.definition: Expressive precision: becoming better able to say what one means
targets.candidate_contributors: Identifying the exact distinction; choosing discriminating words; adding required qualifications; replacing vague reference with a concrete case.
targets.conditions: More technical terminology is useful only when it preserves something consequential for the recipient.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Connection
targets.definition: Connection: relating pieces previously considered separately
targets.candidate_contributors: Juxtaposing relevant elements; identifying a common entity, relation, or dependency; a question requiring joint consideration.
targets.conditions: Association is not automatically dependence; specify what the connection permits one to infer or do.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Disconnection
targets.definition: Disconnection: rejecting a relationship previously assumed
targets.candidate_contributors: A counterexample to the alleged relation; recognition of a common cause; revised scope; independent variation between the elements.
targets.conditions: Failure to detect a relation does not prove absence when the observation is insensitive.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Dependency
targets.definition: Dependency: recognizing what requires what
targets.candidate_contributors: Tracing required inputs; removing a suspected prerequisite in a model or case; identifying what fails when it is absent.
targets.conditions: A habitual predecessor is not necessarily a requirement; alternative routes may satisfy the same need.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Causality
targets.definition: Causality: changing what is understood to produce or influence what
targets.candidate_contributors: Temporal and mechanistic information; intervention contrasts; separation of common causes; comparison of competing causal accounts.
targets.conditions: Observation alone may leave direction and confounding unresolved; a causal label does not resolve them.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Analogy
targets.definition: Analogy: recognizing a transferable relationship across different cases
targets.candidate_contributors: Aligning relations rather than surface features; mapping corresponding roles; identifying where the mapping fails.
targets.conditions: Analogical comparison supported transfer in specific negotiation tasks [S09]; mapped similarity does not prove identical mechanisms.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Composition
targets.definition: Composition: understanding what an arrangement enables together
targets.candidate_contributors: Connecting outputs to required inputs; specifying interfaces; considering interactions, shared constraints, and failure propagation.
targets.conditions: Useful parts may interfere when combined; composition needs more than a list of components.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Part and whole
targets.definition: Part and whole: changing the unit through which a matter is understood
targets.candidate_contributors: Changing the unit represented; relating local behavior to collective organization; exposing part-to-whole dependencies.
targets.conditions: A property of parts need not belong to the whole, or conversely.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Order dependence
targets.definition: Order dependence: recognizing that sequence changes what is possible
targets.candidate_contributors: Comparing alternative sequences; exposing prerequisites; identifying irreversible transitions or intermediate states.
targets.conditions: Order matters only through a specified dependence; a preferred sequence is not thereby necessary.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Level distinction
targets.definition: Level distinction: separating explanations or operations at different scales
targets.candidate_contributors: Separating implementation, function, individual, interaction, and collective descriptions; stating correspondence between levels.
targets.conditions: Changing vocabulary across levels can leave the same unanswered question concealed.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Constraint relation
targets.definition: Constraint relation: recognizing what limits, permits, or redirects an operation
targets.candidate_contributors: Identifying a limit or enabling condition; a boundary case; changing a constraint and deriving the resulting option set.
targets.conditions: An assumed constraint may be negotiable; a physically binding one cannot be removed by redescription alone.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Problem recognition
targets.definition: Problem recognition: something coming to count as requiring a response
targets.candidate_contributors: A consequential mismatch between current and wanted conditions; a previously unseen cost; recognition of preventable failure; a newly available standard.
targets.conditions: Discomfort alone does not identify what needs changing; the relevant discrepancy must be specified.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Problem dissolution
targets.definition: Problem dissolution: an apparent problem ceasing to require the assumed response
targets.candidate_contributors: Removal of a false premise; discovery that the desired condition already holds; withdrawal of an unnecessary requirement; a representation that eliminates the apparent conflict.
targets.conditions: Renaming an unresolved difficulty does not dissolve it; show which demand or contradiction disappears.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Target revision
targets.definition: Target revision: changing what is actually under examination
targets.candidate_contributors: A separating case revealing the wrong object of inquiry; a missing downstream result; an explicit correction of the intended contribution.
targets.conditions: Preserve work that remains relevant, while reopening conclusions that depended on the old target.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Scope revision
targets.definition: Scope revision: changing the boundary of the matter
targets.candidate_contributors: A dependency outside the current boundary; a case excluded without justification; removal of irrelevant surrounding issues.
targets.conditions: Broader scope can reduce tractability; narrower scope must retain the conditions needed for the intended result.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Unit revision
targets.definition: Unit revision: changing whether an individual, interaction, or larger system is examined
targets.candidate_contributors: Evidence that the outcome depends on interaction or organization; comparison of individual and collective explanations; changing the measured entity.
targets.conditions: An individual-level intervention cannot be assumed to alter a collective dependency.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Timescale revision
targets.definition: Timescale revision: changing the interval over which adequacy is considered
targets.candidate_contributors: Delayed effects; persistence requirements; cumulative costs; recovery or recurrence; a decision whose consequences extend beyond the current interval.
targets.conditions: Immediate relief and later benefit may differ; specify whose outcome and which interval matter.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Constraint revision
targets.definition: Constraint revision: changing what is treated as fixed or alterable
targets.candidate_contributors: Evidence that a limit is negotiable; an alternative resource or route; a changed requirement; a physical or institutional restriction previously omitted.
targets.conditions: Distinguish genuinely altered conditions from merely imagining their absence.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Attribution revision
targets.definition: Attribution revision: changing where the difficulty is located
targets.candidate_contributors: A failure trace locating the missing input or operation; comparison across people and situations; evidence against the initial explanation.
targets.conditions: A new blame target is not a causal explanation; identify what difference its alteration would make.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Requirement revision
targets.definition: Requirement revision: changing what would count as resolving the matter
targets.candidate_contributors: Clarification of what the result must enable; discovery of a missing consumer; removal of an unnecessary completion demand; changed user purpose.
targets.conditions: A weaker requirement can make the work complete without making the original objective achieved.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Problem connection
targets.definition: Problem connection: recognizing that several apparent problems share a dependency
targets.candidate_contributors: Tracing several failures to a shared resource, assumption, interface, or criterion; contrasting independent and common causes.
targets.conditions: Common wording does not establish a shared dependency; a joint intervention may leave separate causes intact.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Question formation
targets.definition: Question formation: becoming able to ask a previously unavailable question
targets.candidate_contributors: A newly available distinction; a contradiction; an unexplained contrast; a goal requiring an undetermined input.
targets.conditions: A grammatically formed question may still have no determinate target or answer condition.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Gap recognition
targets.definition: Gap recognition: identifying what remains undetermined
targets.candidate_contributors: Comparing available information with what an operation requires; naming an unresolved variable, alternative, relation, or boundary.
targets.conditions: A generic admission of uncertainty does not identify the missing contribution.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Question replacement
targets.definition: Question replacement: seeing that a different determination is needed
targets.candidate_contributors: Showing that possible answers would leave the actual decision unchanged; identifying a prerequisite determination; exposing a false presupposition.
targets.conditions: Changing the question must preserve or explicitly revise the underlying purpose.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Question priority
targets.definition: Question priority: changing which uncertainty is worth addressing first
targets.candidate_contributors: The consequence of resolving each uncertainty; dependency order; available discriminating information; cost of delay or inquiry.
targets.conditions: The easiest or most interesting question may have little effect on the current activity.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Answerability
targets.definition: Answerability: recognizing what could or could not settle a question
targets.candidate_contributors: A defined result type; an available observation or derivation that separates alternatives; recognition of inaccessible data or incompatible premises.
targets.conditions: Lack of a current answer is different from impossibility in principle.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Evidence requirement
targets.definition: Evidence requirement: changing what information would bear on the inquiry
targets.candidate_contributors: Competing accounts that predict different observations; identifying relevant units and scope; distinguishing testimony, measurement, and derivation.
targets.conditions: More information is useful only if it bears on the unresolved alternatives.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Investigation direction
targets.definition: Investigation direction: changing where an inquiry should proceed
targets.candidate_contributors: A newly exposed dependency; a source with the missing information; a derivable consequence; an informative failure of the current route.
targets.conditions: Continue from the unresolved relation, not from the mere availability of another source.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Completion judgment
targets.definition: Completion judgment: changing whether the inquiry is sufficiently resolved
targets.candidate_contributors: A result satisfying the stated use; elimination or containment of consequential uncertainty; recognition of changed completion criteria.
targets.conditions: Artifact completion is not inquiry completion; residual uncertainty may be acceptable for one use and not another.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Acquisition
targets.definition: Acquisition: coming to accept a previously unaccepted proposition
targets.candidate_contributors: Direct observation; credible testimony; a valid derivation; an interpretation that organizes evidence; repetition or social influence that increases acceptance.
targets.conditions: These routes change acceptance differently; acceptance through familiarity need not add justification.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Rejection
targets.definition: Rejection: ceasing to accept a proposition
targets.candidate_contributors: A decisive counterexample; invalidated support; a stronger incompatible account; recognition that prior acceptance exceeded the grounds.
targets.conditions: Loss of one argument need not establish the proposition's falsity.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Suspension
targets.definition: Suspension: withholding judgment where a commitment was previously made
targets.candidate_contributors: Balanced unresolved alternatives; discovery of unreliable evidence; inability to discriminate at the needed scope; explicit separation of assumption from conclusion.
targets.conditions: Suspension should preserve what remains established rather than erase all distinctions.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Correction
targets.definition: Correction: replacing a mistaken proposition with a better-supported one
targets.candidate_contributors: Identification of the exact false claim; reliable replacement information; explanation of the error-producing step; revision of dependent conclusions.
targets.conditions: A correction that leaves the original causal account intact may fail to change its later use.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Elaboration
targets.definition: Elaboration: adding qualified detail to an existing account
targets.candidate_contributors: Newly warranted conditions, mechanisms, cases, or exceptions; integration with compatible existing knowledge.
targets.conditions: Adding plausible detail without evidence can make an account less accurate while sounding more complete.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Scope restriction
targets.definition: Scope restriction: narrowing where a belief is taken to hold
targets.candidate_contributors: Counterexamples outside a narrower domain; an identified precondition; evidence that a result depends on population, setting, or task.
targets.conditions: Restriction can preserve a useful local claim; it should not conceal an independently false part.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Scope extension
targets.definition: Scope extension: extending a claim where support warrants it
targets.candidate_contributors: Evidence from additional cases; an invariance argument; shared operative conditions; justified transfer across settings.
targets.conditions: Analogy or success in one new case alone may leave broader generalization unresolved.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Inconsistency recognition
