targets.definition: Inconsistency recognition: noticing incompatible commitments
targets.candidate_contributors: Making commitments jointly explicit; aligning definitions, times, and scopes; deriving their incompatible consequences.
targets.conditions: Apparently conflicting sentences may concern different conditions; establish the actual contradiction.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Justification
targets.definition: Justification: gaining or losing grounds for a belief
targets.candidate_contributors: New or withdrawn evidence; source reliability information; a valid inference; exposure of circularity or an unsupported premise.
targets.conditions: More reasons are not necessarily more independent support.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Knowledge integration
targets.definition: Knowledge integration: making a known fact relevant to other commitments
targets.candidate_contributors: Tracing implications into another judgment; connecting a fact to an active decision; revising dependent expectations or actions.
targets.conditions: A fact can be verbally known while remaining absent from the operation it should govern.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Confidence increase
targets.definition: Confidence increase: becoming more certain of a proposition or judgment
targets.candidate_contributors: Discriminating evidence; successful relevant performance; convergence of independent sources; repeated familiarity or authoritative presentation.
targets.conditions: The last two can feel persuasive without adding independent grounds; confidence increase alone is not improvement.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Confidence decrease
targets.definition: Confidence decrease: becoming less certain of a proposition or judgment
targets.candidate_contributors: A failed prediction; credible contradiction; exposed missing knowledge; recognition that evidence is dependent or out of scope.
targets.conditions: An irrelevant challenge can lower confidence without improving its correspondence to support.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Calibration
targets.definition: Calibration: bringing expressed confidence into better correspondence with support or performance
targets.candidate_contributors: Comparing prior confidence with resolved outcomes; separating domains and conditions; revising overused cues; distinguishing evidence strength from ease of response.
targets.conditions: Calibration is a pattern across appropriate cases, not one confident or humble statement.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Possibility recognition
targets.definition: Possibility recognition: treating an excluded alternative as possible
targets.candidate_contributors: A coherent witness or construction; removal of an invalid exclusion; a case that satisfies the relevant constraints.
targets.conditions: Conceivability alone does not establish physical, practical, or institutional possibility.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Impossibility recognition
targets.definition: Impossibility recognition: excluding an alternative for an adequate reason
targets.candidate_contributors: Contradictory requirements; a proven limit; exhaustive exclusion within a finite defined space; absence of a necessary condition.
targets.conditions: Failure to imagine or find an alternative is not a proof of impossibility.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Probability revision
targets.definition: Probability revision: changing relative expectations among alternatives
targets.candidate_contributors: New diagnostic evidence; corrected base rates; information about dependence between observations; revised alternatives or likelihoods.
targets.conditions: A probability shift needs a defined event and reference conditions; vividness does not supply a frequency.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Uncertainty localization
targets.definition: Uncertainty localization: identifying exactly what is unknown
targets.candidate_contributors: Decomposing the account into known and unknown parts; identifying competing explanations; naming unavailable measurements or assumptions.
targets.conditions: An uncertainty label must specify what remains open and what consequence depends on it.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Uncertainty tolerance
targets.definition: Uncertainty tolerance: becoming more or less able to proceed without closure
targets.candidate_contributors: A workable action that tolerates several outcomes; bounded exposure to error; available revision or reversal; permission to retain an unresolved judgment.
targets.conditions: Proceeding without closure differs from pretending the uncertainty is gone.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Confidence differentiation
targets.definition: Confidence differentiation: assigning different certainty to parts of one account
targets.candidate_contributors: Separating observations, interpretations, forecasts, and value judgments; attaching each to its own grounds.
targets.conditions: A single overall confidence can hide a weak link that determines the conclusion.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Reliance threshold
targets.definition: Reliance threshold: changing how much support is required before acting
targets.candidate_contributors: Consequences of a mistaken action; reversibility; delay cost; alternative information; dependence on the claim.
targets.conditions: Changing the threshold is a decision change, not necessarily a change in the proposition's probability.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Mechanism understanding
targets.definition: Mechanism understanding: recognizing how a process produces its effects
targets.candidate_contributors: Tracing entities, transformations, and intermediate states; a worked causal sequence; comparison with an alternative mechanism.
targets.conditions: Mechanism words without intermediate relations leave the explanatory work undone.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Cause revision
targets.definition: Cause revision: changing the attributed cause of an event
targets.candidate_contributors: An intervention contrast; changed temporal or contextual evidence; a competing account explaining the same occurrence; discovery of confounding.
targets.conditions: A better-fitting account may still leave causal identification incomplete.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Multiple causation
targets.definition: Multiple causation: recognizing several contributing conditions
targets.candidate_contributors: Cases with different combinations of conditions; interaction between contributors; separation of triggers, enabling conditions, and maintaining processes.
targets.conditions: A list of factors does not specify whether they add, interact, substitute, or jointly suffice.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Person and situation
targets.definition: Person and situation: changing the relative role assigned to traits and circumstances
targets.candidate_contributors: Comparing the same person across situations and different people in one situation; information about incentives, constraints, and available knowledge.
targets.conditions: Neither trait nor situation should become a universal explanation; interactions may matter.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Intention attribution
targets.definition: Intention attribution: changing what an action is understood to have aimed at
targets.candidate_contributors: The actor's account; observed choices among alternatives; knowledge of their available information; consistency between stated aims and conduct.
targets.conditions: Intention remains partly uncertain; outcome alone does not reveal what was intended [S12].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Controllability attribution
targets.definition: Controllability attribution: changing what could have been influenced
targets.candidate_contributors: Actual intervention opportunities; available resources and authority; time-sensitive alternatives; distinctions between influence and guarantee.
targets.conditions: Hindsight can introduce options unavailable at the time.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Responsibility attribution
targets.definition: Responsibility attribution: changing who or what is held responsible
targets.candidate_contributors: Causal contribution; knowledge and foreseeability; obligations and authority; available alternatives; control over the relevant action.
targets.conditions: Causal involvement, moral blame, and assigned duty are different determinations.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Chance attribution
targets.definition: Chance attribution: changing what is treated as accident rather than regularity
targets.candidate_contributors: A suitable chance model; repeated comparable observations; variation expected under that model; recognition of selection effects.
targets.conditions: An unlikely event alone does not establish a systematic cause or eliminate one.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Explanatory limitation
targets.definition: Explanatory limitation: recognizing what an account leaves unexplained
targets.candidate_contributors: A case the explanation cannot distinguish; an omitted variable or transformation; a circular step; a failed scope extension.
targets.conditions: Admitting that an account is incomplete is useful when it identifies the unresolved dependency.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Inference permission
targets.definition: Inference permission: recognizing that a conclusion does or does not follow
targets.candidate_contributors: Explicit premises and inference rules; a countermodel; distinction between necessary and sufficient conditions; corrected quantifier scope.
targets.conditions: A compelling example can illustrate a conclusion without licensing the inference.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Deductive competence
targets.definition: Deductive competence: becoming able to derive a consequence from premises
targets.candidate_contributors: Worked derivations; performance of individual transformations; correction at the invalid step; practice with structurally different premises.
targets.conditions: Recognizing a valid proof and constructing one require different operations.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Inductive judgment
targets.definition: Inductive judgment: changing how examples support a generalization
targets.candidate_contributors: Representative and contrary examples; sample size and selection information; variability; a specified population of generalization.
targets.conditions: Repeated dependent examples do not contribute like independent representative observations.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Abductive judgment
targets.definition: Abductive judgment: changing which explanation best accounts for observations
targets.candidate_contributors: Alternative mechanisms; their discriminating predictions; fit to all relevant evidence; scope and unsupported assumptions.
targets.conditions: The best available explanation may remain inadequate in absolute terms.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Probabilistic judgment
targets.definition: Probabilistic judgment: changing how uncertain evidence is combined
targets.candidate_contributors: A defined event space; frequencies with consistent denominators; explicit conditional relationships; a diagram or calculation exposing dependence.
targets.conditions: A convenient representation must preserve the actual probabilities and sampling process.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Causal reasoning
targets.definition: Causal reasoning: separating observation, intervention, and causal inference
targets.candidate_contributors: Distinguishing seeing an event from setting it; mapping common causes; an intervention or justified identification argument.
targets.conditions: Prediction from observed associations can succeed even when the proposed intervention fails.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Counterexample use
targets.definition: Counterexample use: recognizing what a contrary case actually defeats
targets.candidate_contributors: A contrary case satisfying the claim's antecedent and scope; identification of the precise universal or necessity claim it contradicts.
targets.conditions: A case outside the claim's conditions is not a counterexample to it.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Assumption tracking
targets.definition: Assumption tracking: preserving the conditions on which a conclusion depends
targets.candidate_contributors: An explicit dependency record; tagging provisional premises; carrying conditions into derived statements; reopening conclusions after premise revision.
targets.conditions: A qualification placed elsewhere is ineffective if the dependent conclusion is reused without it.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Consistency maintenance
targets.definition: Consistency maintenance: reconciling or separating conflicting commitments
targets.candidate_contributors: Jointly inspecting commitments; distinguishing genuine contradiction from different scopes; retracting or qualifying the unsupported dependency.
targets.conditions: Consistency alone does not establish truth; many mutually consistent accounts may remain possible.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Error correction
targets.definition: Error correction: identifying and repairing a mistaken reasoning operation
targets.candidate_contributors: Locating the mistaken operation; supplying a valid replacement; recomputing dependent steps; preserving independently supported results.
targets.conditions: A corrected final sentence can still be generated by an unchanged faulty method.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Outcome expectation
targets.definition: Outcome expectation: changing what is expected to happen
targets.candidate_contributors: Observed outcomes; a causal model; credible advance information; changed resources or constraints; comparison with similar cases.
targets.conditions: Expectation should concern a defined event; wanting or fearing it supplies different information.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Timing expectation
targets.definition: Timing expectation: changing when something is expected
targets.candidate_contributors: Event schedules; observed timing distributions; elapsed time and stage indicators; a changed dependency on earlier events.
targets.conditions: Average timing can conceal wide variability and conditional delays.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Action dependence
targets.definition: Action dependence: recognizing how alternatives lead to different possible consequences
targets.candidate_contributors: Tracing consequences of each available action; identifying branching conditions; comparison with inaction; accounting for others' responses.
targets.conditions: Simulating consequences does not establish their likelihood or feasibility.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Response anticipation
targets.definition: Response anticipation: representing how another person or system may respond
targets.candidate_contributors: The recipient's actual statements and behavior; response histories under similar conditions; known interface rules; unresolved alternative interpretations.
targets.conditions: Imagining a viewpoint can increase confidence without improving accuracy; direct perspective-getting helped in studied human tasks [S12].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Preparation recognition
targets.definition: Preparation recognition: seeing what must be available before a future condition
targets.candidate_contributors: Working backward from a future operation to its required inputs; setup duration; deadlines; an unavailable resource that must be obtained earlier.
targets.conditions: Preparation matters only if its result survives and is accessible when required.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Contingency awareness
targets.definition: Contingency awareness: recognizing that different outcomes require different continuations
targets.candidate_contributors: Distinct outcome branches; observable triggers; a feasible continuation for each consequential branch; a fallback for unresolved cases.
targets.conditions: An enormous scenario list can obscure the few differences that alter the next action.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Surprise
targets.definition: Surprise: encountering a mismatch between expectation and occurrence
targets.candidate_contributors: A specific prior expectation; a perceived deviation; novelty or violation of an inferred regularity.
targets.conditions: Surprise establishes mismatch with an expectation, not necessarily importance or objective improbability.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Expectation separation
targets.definition: Expectation separation: distinguishing hoped-for, feared, possible, and likely outcomes
targets.candidate_contributors: Separating desire, dread, logical possibility, forecast, and commitment; attaching each to its proper grounds.
targets.conditions: An emotionally vivid simulation can migrate into a forecast unless these roles remain distinct.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Expectation influence
targets.definition: Expectation influence: recognizing that expressing an expectation can affect what follows
targets.candidate_contributors: A communicated forecast changing attention, effort, coordination, or treatment; awareness of how others respond to the forecast.
targets.conditions: Prediction can be an intervention; a changed outcome may reflect that response rather than the original forecast's accuracy.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Image construction
targets.definition: Image construction: forming a previously unavailable mental scene
targets.candidate_contributors: Recombining remembered sensory elements; spatial instructions; a concrete scene description; an external image serving as a construction aid.
targets.conditions: People differ in imagery experience; understanding a scene does not require the same subjective image.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Vividness
targets.definition: Vividness: making an imagined scene more or less experientially detailed
targets.candidate_contributors: Adding sensory particulars; specifying viewpoint, movement, and sequence; sustained attention to selected features; reducing or abstracting scene detail.
targets.conditions: Vividness can increase apparent plausibility without changing the scenario's support.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Possibility construction
targets.definition: Possibility construction: conceiving an alternative not previously represented
targets.candidate_contributors: Combining available elements differently; identifying an overlooked actor or action; relaxing an assumed constraint; introducing a new resource.
targets.conditions: A represented possibility requires a separate feasibility account before reliance.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Counterfactual construction
targets.definition: Counterfactual construction: representing how things could have been otherwise
targets.candidate_contributors: Selecting a changeable antecedent; varying it while retaining relevant background conditions; tracing the alternative consequences.
targets.conditions: Changing everything at once prevents attribution of the imagined difference to the selected change.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Perspective taking
targets.definition: Perspective taking: imagining a situation from another position
targets.candidate_contributors: Information about another position's access, aims, history, and constraints; representing what is visible from that position; checking against the person's account.
targets.conditions: Imagination supplies a candidate model of another mind, not direct access to it [S12].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Future simulation
targets.definition: Future simulation: constructing a possible later situation
targets.candidate_contributors: A specified future time and situation; present dependencies carried forward; plausible branches; concrete details connecting actions to consequences.
targets.conditions: One detailed future can crowd out other plausible futures.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Recombination
targets.definition: Recombination: bringing elements together in an unfamiliar arrangement
targets.candidate_contributors: A repertoire of components; alternative ways of joining them; cross-domain examples; a purpose that makes an unusual combination consequential.
targets.conditions: Combinations need compatible interfaces; novelty of assembly does not establish usefulness.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Constraint variation
targets.definition: Constraint variation: imagining what changes when a supposed constraint changes
targets.candidate_contributors: Naming the assumed constraint; replacing its value or status; deriving which options and dependencies change.
targets.conditions: Relaxing one constraint can reveal another; no inference follows from an unspecified 'anything is possible' premise.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Provisional adoption
targets.definition: Provisional adoption: using an interpretation without committing to its truth
targets.candidate_contributors: An explicit temporary assumption; a bounded task in which to use it; preserving the original alternatives; a condition for withdrawal.
targets.conditions: Provisional use becomes misleading if later outputs omit its assumed status.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Simulation control
targets.definition: Simulation control: changing the ability to enter, alter, or leave an imagined scenario
targets.candidate_contributors: Entry and exit cues; control over scenario variables; external scene descriptions; an available shift to current sensory or task information.
targets.conditions: Ability to describe control does not establish voluntary control over all imagery or intrusive content.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Idea availability
targets.definition: Idea availability: gaining access to an idea not previously considered
targets.candidate_contributors: A cue linked to unused knowledge; a changed representation; exposure to a relevant unfamiliar example; a question exposing a missing relation.
targets.conditions: An idea can be new to this moment while already existing in the person's repertoire.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Fluency
targets.definition: Fluency: changing how readily candidate ideas can be produced
targets.candidate_contributors: Successive prompts along different dimensions; loosening premature selection; access to examples; changing activity or setting.
targets.conditions: Walking increased divergent generation in specific tasks, without uniform gains on convergent tasks [S13].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Diversity
targets.definition: Diversity: producing candidates that differ in consequential ways
targets.candidate_contributors: Varying mechanism, target, resource, sequence, or scope; detecting duplicate assumptions; constructing alternatives with different consequences.
targets.conditions: Different wording is insufficient diversity when every candidate preserves the same operative choice.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Originality
targets.definition: Originality: constructing an idea new relative to a specified prior repertoire
targets.candidate_contributors: Comparing with the specified prior repertoire; changing a core relation; combining previously unjoined elements; inventing a new operation.
targets.conditions: Originality is relative to a reference set; lack of recognition does not establish historical novelty.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Constraint transformation
targets.definition: Constraint transformation: changing the structure within which an invention is sought
targets.candidate_contributors: Reframing the desired function; replacing a fixed means; changing the unit of design; exploiting a limit as a design feature.
targets.conditions: A changed problem may produce something inventive that no longer serves the original purpose.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Remote connection
targets.definition: Remote connection: identifying a useful relation between distant matters
targets.candidate_contributors: A shared relation across distant domains; explicit role mapping; a need in one domain supplied by a mechanism in another.
targets.conditions: Distance alone adds no value; the transferred relation must survive consequential differences [S09].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Elaboration
targets.definition: Elaboration: developing an initial idea into a more articulated possibility
targets.candidate_contributors: Supplying missing components, interfaces, conditions, examples, and consequences; resolving underspecified choices.
targets.conditions: Elaboration can expose infeasibility rather than improve the idea; retain that discovery.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Creative selection
targets.definition: Creative selection: recognizing which idea deserves further development
targets.candidate_contributors: Comparison against the actual purpose; feasibility constraints; consequences that distinguish candidates; development cost; available evidence.
targets.conditions: An attractive presentation can dominate attention while contributing little to the design criterion.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Creative confidence
targets.definition: Creative confidence: changing willingness to construct or express unfamiliar ideas
targets.candidate_contributors: A successful act of original construction; a setting permitting unfinished attempts; specific recognition of a useful contribution; separating proposal from endorsement.
targets.conditions: Encouragement without opportunity or skill may raise willingness without improving construction.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Comprehension
targets.definition: Comprehension: making sense of previously opaque material
targets.candidate_contributors: Resolving unknown terms; a concrete example; showing the governing relation; supplying a missing prerequisite; reducing irrelevant representational load.
targets.conditions: Smooth reading is insufficient evidence of comprehension; the needed use determines what must become available.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Integration
targets.definition: Integration: understanding how formerly separate pieces fit together
targets.candidate_contributors: Mapping correspondences between pieces; resolving incompatible assumptions; showing their shared dependency; constructing a combined example.
targets.conditions: Combining statements without reconciling their conditions can create superficial coherence.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Consequence access
targets.definition: Consequence access: becoming able to derive what an account implies
targets.candidate_contributors: Making premises available; performing the missing inference; a contrast revealing what changes downstream; carrying qualifications into the result.
targets.conditions: Restating the premise leaves consequence access unchanged when the recipient already knows it.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Operational understanding
targets.definition: Operational understanding: becoming able to use an account in an activity
targets.candidate_contributors: A worked application; executable steps; required resources; an attempt on a relevant case; correction at the failed operation.
targets.conditions: A description of use does not supply every motor, social, or cognitive ability needed to perform it.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Boundary understanding
targets.definition: Boundary understanding: recognizing when an account does not apply
targets.candidate_contributors: An inapplicable near neighbor; a violated precondition; an exception; comparison of successful and unsuccessful uses.
targets.conditions: Knowing an example's failure does not identify the boundary unless the relevant difference is isolated.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Insight
targets.definition: Insight: reorganizing a matter so a previously inaccessible relationship becomes apparent
targets.candidate_contributors: A representation exposing an overlooked relation; abandoning a blocking assumption; joining previously separated information; a separating case.
targets.conditions: The felt suddenness of insight does not establish accuracy or explain how the reorganization occurred.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Illusion of understanding
targets.definition: Illusion of understanding: becoming confident in understanding without the corresponding ability
targets.candidate_contributors: Fluent explanations; familiar terms; repeated exposure; a persuasive narrative; absence of a demand to reconstruct missing steps.
targets.conditions: These are possible sources of misplaced confidence; feeling able to explain can exceed actual explanatory performance [S14].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Understanding correction
targets.definition: Understanding correction: recognizing and repairing that mismatch
targets.candidate_contributors: Attempting the required explanation or operation; locating the missing step; supplying its relation or input; reconstructing the account afterward.
targets.conditions: Exposing a gap reduces an illusion only if the person recognizes the mismatch; repair is additional work [S14].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Explanatory independence
targets.definition: Explanatory independence: becoming able to reconstruct an understanding without repeating its wording
targets.candidate_contributors: Rebuilding from premises; expressing the relation in another form; producing a fresh example; answering a novel consequence question.
targets.conditions: Paraphrase alone may preserve memorized wording without independent reconstruction.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Concern formation
targets.definition: Concern formation: something coming to matter
targets.candidate_contributors: Encountering a consequential need or possibility; an emotionally meaningful experience; recognizing effects on someone valued; adopting a commitment.
targets.conditions: Attention to a concern and durable valuation differ; a vivid episode may have temporary influence.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Concern reduction
targets.definition: Concern reduction: something ceasing to matter as much
targets.candidate_contributors: Resolution of a need; changed relevance; revised interpretation of the cost; competing concerns; repeated disappointment or disengagement.
targets.conditions: Reduced concern can reflect relief, informed reprioritization, or loss of responsiveness; these require different interpretation.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Value priority
targets.definition: Value priority: changing which concern takes precedence
targets.candidate_contributors: A concrete conflict between concerns; changed consequences; reflection on accepted sacrifices; a commitment that orders competing demands.
targets.conditions: Stated priority may differ from choices under cost; neither automatically captures a context-free permanent value.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Intrinsic valuation
targets.definition: Intrinsic valuation: changing what is valued for its own sake
targets.candidate_contributors: Direct experience of the activity or object; appreciation of its qualities; identification with its practice; changing its felt meaning.
targets.conditions: Removing external rewards does not by itself establish that intrinsic valuation will increase.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Instrumental valuation
targets.definition: Instrumental valuation: changing what is valued for what it enables
targets.candidate_contributors: A newly visible means-end relation; changed effectiveness or cost; an alternative serving the same end; loss of the original goal.
targets.conditions: Instrumental value can disappear when its dependency disappears while other kinds of value remain.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Concern scope
targets.definition: Concern scope: extending or narrowing who or what counts
targets.candidate_contributors: Attention to previously excluded people, entities, consequences, or future periods; recognition of shared features; revised inclusion criteria.
targets.conditions: A widened description does not prove that the included concerns now govern choices.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Value conflict recognition
targets.definition: Value conflict recognition: noticing incompatible or competing concerns
targets.candidate_contributors: Presenting incompatible requirements together; revealing a shared scarce resource; showing that one action advances one concern while obstructing another.
targets.conditions: A conflict may be contingent on the available options rather than inherent in the values.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Value reconciliation
targets.definition: Value reconciliation: finding a way to relate concerns without the former conflict
targets.candidate_contributors: Separating means from ends; finding a compatible alternative; allocating by circumstance or time; revising an unnecessary requirement.
targets.conditions: Some conflicts remain real; reconciliation cannot be established by renaming a sacrifice.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Value enactment
targets.definition: Value enactment: changing whether acknowledged values govern actual choices
targets.candidate_contributors: A decision rule expressing the value; point-of-choice access to its consequence; resources and authority to act; removal of conflicting defaults.
targets.conditions: Changes in enactment may arise without changes in underlying valuation.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Preference formation
targets.definition: Preference formation: developing a preference where none was settled
targets.candidate_contributors: Experience with alternatives; comparison on newly noticed qualities; social examples; a choice that reveals a previously unspecified concern.
targets.conditions: A selection can reflect availability, framing, or compromise rather than a stable ranking.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Preference reversal
targets.definition: Preference reversal: changing the ranking of alternatives
targets.candidate_contributors: Changed consequences or context; new information; altered reference points; satiation; a different representation of the same options.
targets.conditions: Presentation alone can reverse choices in studied framing problems [S11]; reversal need not establish changed underlying interests.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Attraction
targets.definition: Attraction: becoming more or less drawn to an object or activity
targets.candidate_contributors: Appealing sensory properties; anticipated reward; familiarity or novelty; meaningful association; an opportunity aligned with current need.
targets.conditions: Attraction can change independently of considered endorsement or actual benefit.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Aversion
targets.definition: Aversion: becoming more or less repelled by it
targets.candidate_contributors: Unpleasant experience; anticipated harm or effort; learned associations; conflicting values; repeated unwanted exposure.
targets.conditions: Avoidance can preserve an aversion by preventing relevant corrective experience, but not every aversion is mistaken.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Taste discrimination
targets.definition: Taste discrimination: noticing distinctions that change appreciation
targets.candidate_contributors: Contrasting similar works or experiences; vocabulary for consequential features; directed attention to composition, technique, or texture.
targets.conditions: Learning to describe differences does not prescribe which should be liked.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Aesthetic appreciation
targets.definition: Aesthetic appreciation: coming to perceive beauty, elegance, ugliness, or expressive force
targets.candidate_contributors: Encountering form, contrast, rhythm, or expressive relation; contextual knowledge; a newly available interpretation; sustained perceptual attention.
targets.conditions: Appreciation is recipient- and context-dependent; expertise need not converge on one ranking.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Familiarity preference
targets.definition: Familiarity preference: changing attraction associated with familiarity
targets.candidate_contributors: Repeated encounters; easier identification and processing; positive associations; reduced uncertainty about the object.
targets.conditions: Familiarity may become boredom or aversion; repeated exposure is not universally attractive.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Novelty preference
targets.definition: Novelty preference: changing attraction associated with unfamiliarity
targets.candidate_contributors: A contrast with a saturated repertoire; uncertainty promising discovery; lower expected risk; access to an unfamiliar but interpretable experience.
targets.conditions: Novelty can also impose confusion or threat; its value depends on the current concern and capacity.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Preference independence
targets.definition: Preference independence: becoming less dependent on another person's stated preference
targets.candidate_contributors: Firsthand examination; forming criteria before seeing others' ratings; separate judgments before discussion; identifying conformity pressure.
targets.conditions: Independence need not mean rejecting useful expertise; the question is what grounds the preference.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Wanting
targets.definition: Wanting: changing the pull of an anticipated object or outcome
targets.candidate_contributors: Reward-predicting cues; current deprivation or need; opportunity proximity; imagery of attainment; learned incentive associations.
targets.conditions: Wanting can persist without enjoyment; desire intensity is not a measure of benefit.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Liking
targets.definition: Liking: changing enjoyment during an experience
targets.candidate_contributors: The consumed or encountered experience; sensory quality; satiation; current bodily state; attention to pleasant or unpleasant features.
targets.conditions: Anticipated pleasure and experienced pleasure can differ; observation of pursuit does not establish liking.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Anticipated reward
targets.definition: Anticipated reward: changing the expected benefit of an activity
targets.candidate_contributors: Outcome information; remembered experience; a credible path to attainment; revised probability, magnitude, or timing of the benefit.
targets.conditions: A more vivid reward may feel larger without becoming more likely or valuable.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Satisfaction
targets.definition: Satisfaction: changing how fulfilled or disappointed an outcome feels
targets.candidate_contributors: Comparison of outcome with expectations and requirements; attention to what was obtained or missed; satiation; changing comparison standards.
targets.conditions: Lowering expectations can alter satisfaction while leaving the actual outcome unchanged.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Effort valuation
targets.definition: Effort valuation: changing how burdensome effort seems relative to its benefit
targets.candidate_contributors: Task complexity and friction; visible progress; expected payoff; available support; whether effort itself is valued or resented.
targets.conditions: Reducing effort can improve access, while removing valued challenge can reduce engagement.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Delay valuation
targets.definition: Delay valuation: changing the relative weight of earlier and later consequences
targets.candidate_contributors: Making later consequences concrete; credible delivery expectations; a connection to one's future situation; immediate need; alternative uses of resources.
targets.conditions: A vivid future is one possible contributor; laboratory allocation changes do not establish enduring real-world benefit [S23].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Risk valuation
targets.definition: Risk valuation: changing how uncertain gains and losses are weighed
targets.candidate_contributors: Information about probabilities and stakes; gain/loss framing; reference points; ability to absorb adverse outcomes.
targets.conditions: Equivalent descriptions can produce different choices [S11]; a preferred frame is not automatically a better valuation.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Opportunity cost
targets.definition: Opportunity cost: recognizing what another commitment displaces
targets.candidate_contributors: Making the displaced alternative explicit; a common resource budget; the time or attention occupied by the current commitment.
targets.conditions: Only feasible alternatives belong in the immediate opportunity-cost comparison.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Trade-off recognition
targets.definition: Trade-off recognition: seeing what must be given up to obtain something else
targets.candidate_contributors: A comparison exposing incompatible gains; identifying a binding resource; varying one feature while tracking the other consequence.
targets.conditions: A trade-off may disappear with a new design; do not assume the current option set is final.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Sufficiency judgment
targets.definition: Sufficiency judgment: changing when something counts as enough
targets.candidate_contributors: An explicit requirement or saturation point; diminishing additional benefit; displaced opportunities; completion evidence.
targets.conditions: Enough for the stated use and globally optimal are different judgments.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Desire
targets.definition: Desire: developing, strengthening, weakening, or losing a want
targets.candidate_contributors: A newly salient valued outcome; current need; rewarding experience or anticipation; changed associations; loss of appeal through satiation.
targets.conditions: A want can strengthen without becoming a considered goal or a feasible action.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Willingness
targets.definition: Willingness: becoming more or less prepared to undertake an activity
targets.candidate_contributors: An acceptable expected consequence; reduced initiation cost; available ability and support; meaningful choice; tolerable exposure to failure.
targets.conditions: Someone may value an outcome while declining the proposed means for sound reasons.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Approach
targets.definition: Approach: becoming more inclined to move toward a possibility
targets.candidate_contributors: A visible attainable benefit; an available first move; lower perceived threat; prior rewarding contact with the possibility.
targets.conditions: Approach tendency does not establish that the option serves longer-term interests.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Avoidance
targets.definition: Avoidance: becoming more inclined to move away from it
targets.candidate_contributors: Expected harm, loss, humiliation, effort, or incompatibility; learned warning cues; an available exit or alternative.
targets.conditions: Avoidance can be protective or unnecessarily restrictive; identify the actual predicted consequence.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Effort mobilization
targets.definition: Effort mobilization: becoming ready to allocate more or less effort
targets.candidate_contributors: A worthwhile and attainable demand; explicit effort requirements; immediate resources; visible progress; removal of competing commitments.
targets.conditions: More activation cannot compensate for an impossible task or an unavailable prerequisite.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Initiative
targets.definition: Initiative: becoming more or less likely to originate an activity
targets.candidate_contributors: Recognition of an unfilled need; authority to act; ownership of a next step; an accessible starting point; expected consequence of inaction.
targets.conditions: Initiative can be blocked by unclear permission or resources even when motivation is strong.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Commitment to effort
targets.definition: Commitment to effort: changing willingness to work despite difficulty
targets.candidate_contributors: A sustained reason for the work; credible progress; manageable stages; expected value of continued effort; protection from competing demands.
targets.conditions: Continuing through difficulty is beneficial only while the activity still serves its purpose.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Motivational conflict
targets.definition: Motivational conflict: changing the competition among incompatible inclinations
targets.candidate_contributors: Making competing wants explicit; separating immediate and later consequences; finding a compatible alternative; choosing a governing priority.
targets.conditions: A declared priority need not extinguish the competing inclination.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Interest maintenance
targets.definition: Interest maintenance: sustaining or losing engagement with an activity
targets.candidate_contributors: Successive meaningful questions or challenges; increasing capability; variation that retains purpose; access to consequential progress.
targets.conditions: Constant novelty can disrupt cumulative understanding rather than sustain useful interest.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Reason uptake
targets.definition: Reason uptake: a recognized reason beginning or ceasing to affect motivation
targets.candidate_contributors: Connecting the reason to an actual choice; making its consequence concrete; resolving an incompatible commitment; providing a feasible response.
targets.conditions: Agreement with a reason does not ensure it becomes operative under pressure or distraction.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Interest emergence
targets.definition: Interest emergence: a matter becoming worth investigating
targets.candidate_contributors: An unexplained contrast; a personally relevant consequence; a surprising example; recognition of an accessible but missing relation.
targets.conditions: A question must be intelligible enough to engage; total opacity may produce disengagement.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Question appetite
targets.definition: Question appetite: wanting to resolve a particular uncertainty
targets.candidate_contributors: A defined gap between known and wanted information; a plausible route to an answer; anticipated value or enjoyment of discovery.
targets.conditions: Resolving uncertainty can be unhelpful when the information has no relevant use and displaces more important work.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Exploration breadth
targets.definition: Exploration breadth: widening or narrowing what one is willing to examine
targets.candidate_contributors: Distinct exploratory dimensions; access to unfamiliar examples; lower cost of sampling; a purpose requiring wider coverage.
targets.conditions: Breadth without consequential differentiation can produce repetition in disguise.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Novelty approach
targets.definition: Novelty approach: becoming more willing to encounter unfamiliar material
targets.candidate_contributors: A manageable introduction; optional participation; connections to familiar knowledge; visible potential benefit; credible control over exposure.
targets.conditions: Unfamiliarity can remain costly or unwanted; novelty is not an intrinsic improvement criterion.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Ambiguity engagement
targets.definition: Ambiguity engagement: becoming willing to remain with an unresolved matter
targets.candidate_contributors: A meaningful unresolved question; partial structure; permission to defer commitment; a way to preserve progress while uncertainty remains.
targets.conditions: Remaining engaged need not mean repeatedly revisiting the same unproductive operation.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Playfulness
targets.definition: Playfulness: entering an activity with freedom to vary its possibilities
targets.candidate_contributors: Reversible variations; low penalties for imperfect attempts; flexible rules; materials inviting manipulation; separation of exploration from final commitment.
targets.conditions: Play can reveal possibilities without establishing that they work outside the play conditions.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Incidental pursuit
targets.definition: Incidental pursuit: following an unexpected connection
targets.candidate_contributors: Recognition that an unexpected connection could supply a missing contribution; a recoverable record of the original path; available exploration time.
targets.conditions: An interesting tangent needs a plausible relation to the activity or a consciously revised purpose.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Exploration cessation
targets.definition: Exploration cessation: deciding that further exploration is no longer worthwhile
targets.candidate_contributors: No remaining consequential difference among outcomes; declining additional value; a binding resource cost; sufficient material for the next operation.
targets.conditions: Stopping search does not prove exhaustive coverage; retain the scope of what was examined.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Joy
targets.definition: Joy: changes in experienced delight or happiness
targets.candidate_contributors: A welcomed event or encounter; achievement of a valued aim; playful or rewarding experience; attention to an appreciated feature.
targets.conditions: The same event can evoke different feelings depending on its personal meaning and current state.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Sadness and grief
targets.definition: Sadness and grief: changes in felt loss or sorrow
targets.candidate_contributors: Loss or recognition of absence; reminders of attachment; interpretation of what has ended; opportunities to express and share the experience.
targets.conditions: Grief is not simply an erroneous belief to remove; changed expression and changed felt loss may diverge.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Fear
targets.definition: Fear: changes in experienced threat or apprehension
targets.candidate_contributors: A perceived threat; uncertainty about harm; learned warning cues; absence or presence of control, protection, and escape.
targets.conditions: Fear can be warranted or disproportionate; reassurance changes it only through a relation the person can use.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Anger
targets.definition: Anger: changes in felt grievance and readiness to oppose
targets.candidate_contributors: Perceived obstruction, injustice, disrespect, or intentional harm; attribution of responsibility; available means of redress.
targets.conditions: Changing blame can change anger without resolving the actual obstruction or injustice.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Disgust
targets.definition: Disgust: changes in felt revulsion
targets.candidate_contributors: An aversive sensory encounter; contamination cues; learned associations; an interpretation of the object or event.
targets.conditions: Reappraisal and suppression had different experiential and physiological effects in a disgust-film experiment [S17].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Shame
targets.definition: Shame: changes in feeling exposed or diminished before oneself or others
targets.candidate_contributors: Perceived global self-failure; anticipated or actual exposure to devaluation; identification with a condemning judgment; acceptance or rejection by valued others.
targets.conditions: Separating a specific act from total self-worth is a candidate contribution, not a guaranteed emotional effect.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Guilt
targets.definition: Guilt: changes in distress about one's attributed wrongdoing
targets.candidate_contributors: Attributing a harmful act or omission to oneself; recognizing a violated commitment; new evidence about responsibility; possible repair.
targets.conditions: Relieving guilt by changing attribution is appropriate only if the attribution was mistaken or incomplete.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Pride
targets.definition: Pride: changes in satisfaction or esteem concerning oneself or an affiliation
targets.candidate_contributors: A valued achievement; attribution of contribution to oneself or a group; recognition by a respected audience; comparison with a meaningful standard.
targets.conditions: Pride can rest on accurate contribution, inflated attribution, or a borrowed group achievement.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Envy and jealousy
targets.definition: Envy and jealousy: changes in feelings concerning another's advantage or a threatened relationship
targets.candidate_contributors: Comparison with another's advantage; a perceived threat to a valued relationship; uncertainty about inclusion; revised information about loss or exclusivity.
targets.conditions: Envy and jealousy have different objects; neither licenses assumptions about another person's intentions.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Gratitude
targets.definition: Gratitude: changes in felt appreciation for a received benefit
targets.candidate_contributors: Recognizing a received benefit; attributing it to another's contribution or care; making its personal significance available.
targets.conditions: Demanding gratitude can add pressure or resentment; benefit and benevolent intent are separate questions.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Compassion
targets.definition: Compassion: changes in concern for another's suffering
targets.candidate_contributors: Recognizing suffering; understanding its circumstances; perceived connection to the affected person; an available way to help.
targets.conditions: Emotional resonance, concern, and effective assistance can vary independently.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Amusement
targets.definition: Amusement: changes in experiencing something as funny or playful
targets.candidate_contributors: An unexpected but interpretable incongruity; playful framing; timing and shared context; recognition of a benign alternative meaning.
targets.conditions: A mismatch can be amusing to one person and threatening or tedious to another.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Awe
targets.definition: Awe: changes in response to something experienced as vast or beyond the familiar
targets.candidate_contributors: Encountering perceived vastness, complexity, or extraordinary capability; attention to scale; an experience exceeding the current interpretive frame.
targets.conditions: Awe can coexist with fear and need not improve the accuracy of subsequent judgments.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Relief
targets.definition: Relief: changes in feeling that an anticipated burden or threat has eased
targets.candidate_contributors: Evidence that an anticipated threat or burden has diminished; release from an obligation; completion of a difficult requirement.
targets.conditions: Relief can arise from mistaken reassurance; distinguish felt release from actual resolution.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Hope and despair
targets.definition: Hope and despair: changes in emotional orientation toward future possibility
targets.candidate_contributors: A credible route toward or away from a valued possibility; perceived control; support; evidence about remaining options.
targets.conditions: Hope need not require certainty, and severe pessimism does not prove that no route exists.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Frustration
targets.definition: Frustration: changes in felt obstruction of an attempted activity
targets.candidate_contributors: A blocked intended operation; repeated unsuccessful effort; unclear requirements; removal or explanation of the obstruction.
targets.conditions: An explanation can reduce uncertainty while leaving the practical blockage intact.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Regret
targets.definition: Regret: changes in feelings concerning an unrealized alternative
targets.candidate_contributors: A salient unrealized alternative; belief that it was available; comparison of outcomes; revised understanding of what could have been known.
targets.conditions: Hindsight can create regret for a choice whose better alternative was not accessible then.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Mixed emotion
targets.definition: Mixed emotion: changes in the coexistence and balance of multiple emotions
targets.candidate_contributors: Simultaneous consequences for different concerns; different interpretations of one event; attention moving among gains, losses, attachment, and conflict.
targets.conditions: One emotional label may conceal meaningful coexistence rather than indecision or confusion.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Love
targets.definition: Love: changes in felt attachment, care, or devotion
targets.candidate_contributors: Repeated caring interaction; attachment and shared history; responsive attention; valued knowledge of the other; changing trust or separation.
targets.conditions: Love includes distinct experiences and commitments; no message or sequence guarantees it.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Admiration
targets.definition: Admiration: changes in regard for another's qualities or actions
targets.candidate_contributors: Perception of a valued quality in action; understanding the difficulty or contribution involved; comparison with relevant alternatives.
targets.conditions: Prestige or impressive presentation can imitate evidence of an admirable quality.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Embarrassment
targets.definition: Embarrassment: changes in discomfort concerning a socially exposed mishap
targets.candidate_contributors: An exposed mismatch with a social expectation; perceived audience attention; interpretation of the mishap; a response that restores workable participation.
targets.conditions: Actual audience judgment may differ from imagined judgment; public reassurance can sometimes prolong exposure.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Contempt
targets.definition: Contempt: changes in regarding someone or something as beneath consideration
targets.candidate_contributors: Attributing serious inferiority or norm violation; distancing from the target; dehumanizing or dismissive categorization; revised information about the person or act.
targets.conditions: Understanding a cause does not require endorsing contempt; global dismissal can conceal relevant distinctions.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Boredom
targets.definition: Boredom: changes in feeling insufficiently engaged by available activity
targets.candidate_contributors: Insufficient challenge or meaning; repetitive stimulation; inability to engage an available activity; mismatch between demand and capacity.
targets.conditions: Adding stimulation can leave the missing purpose or inaccessible task unchanged.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Longing
targets.definition: Longing: changes in felt desire for an absent person, condition, or possibility
targets.candidate_contributors: Salient absence of a valued person or condition; memory and imagination of contact; perceived distance from attainment; changes in accessibility.
targets.conditions: Fulfillment, acceptance of absence, and replacement of the concern are different possible changes.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Background mood
targets.definition: Background mood: changes in the prevailing affective tone
targets.candidate_contributors: Accumulated daily events; recurring interpretations; sustained bodily state; social environment; sleep and activity patterns.
targets.conditions: A prevailing mood may have multiple maintaining conditions; one conversational event need not reset it.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Valence
targets.definition: Valence: becoming generally more pleasant, unpleasant, or neutral in feeling
targets.candidate_contributors: Pleasant or unpleasant sensory input; appraised gains and losses; current bodily comfort; emotionally meaningful interaction.
targets.conditions: General pleasantness can change while a specific emotion or unresolved concern persists.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Irritability
targets.definition: Irritability: changing readiness to react with annoyance
targets.candidate_contributors: Repeated interruption or obstruction; fatigue; discomfort; perceived disrespect; reduced room to recover between demands.
targets.conditions: The contributor may be environmental or bodily rather than a defective attitude.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Emotional intensity
targets.definition: Emotional intensity: feelings becoming stronger or weaker
targets.candidate_contributors: Perceived magnitude and immediacy of consequences; attention to evocative details; physiological activation; reinterpretation or changed circumstances.
targets.conditions: Stronger expression does not necessarily indicate stronger felt intensity.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Emotional duration
targets.definition: Emotional duration: feelings lasting longer or shorter
targets.candidate_contributors: Continued provoking events; repeated recollection or simulation; unfinished action tendencies; new competing experiences; recognition of an ending.
targets.conditions: Duration can change without changing the initial intensity or the underlying concern.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Emotional variability
targets.definition: Emotional variability: feelings changing more or less readily over time
targets.candidate_contributors: Rapidly changing events or appraisals; shifts of attention; competing concerns; bodily state; repeated social feedback.
targets.conditions: Variability needs an observation interval; a single transition does not characterize a lasting disposition.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Recovery from emotion
targets.definition: Recovery from emotion: returning toward a prior state after an event
targets.candidate_contributors: Ending the precipitating condition; obtaining needed resolution or support; disengaging from repeated activation; restoring ordinary activity.
targets.conditions: Recovery can involve a changed baseline rather than a return to the exact prior state.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Emotional differentiation
targets.definition: Emotional differentiation: experiencing feelings as more distinct or undifferentiated
targets.candidate_contributors: Comparing nearby feelings; attending to distinct bodily, evaluative, and action components; a usable emotional vocabulary; context-specific reflection.
targets.conditions: Vocabulary can become more differentiated without proving equally differentiated experience.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Emotional numbness
targets.definition: Emotional numbness: becoming more or less responsive in felt experience
targets.candidate_contributors: Changes in prolonged overload, disconnection, or bodily state; renewed contact with personally meaningful experiences; changes in attention and appraisal.
targets.conditions: This label covers different mechanisms; the inventory does not diagnose its cause or prescribe treatment.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Emotion recognition
targets.definition: Emotion recognition: noticing what one is feeling
targets.candidate_contributors: Attention to current bodily sensations, appraisals, and action urges; comparison with familiar episodes; a prompt naming an overlooked component.
targets.conditions: Recognizing an emotion is an interpretation that can remain uncertain.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Emotion labeling
targets.definition: Emotion labeling: becoming able to name or distinguish a feeling
targets.candidate_contributors: Words linked to distinguishable experiences; contrast between nearby emotions; descriptions of the event's meaning and action tendency.
targets.conditions: A label can organize experience or constrain it inaccurately; preserve mixed and uncertain cases.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Acceptance
targets.definition: Acceptance: changing willingness to experience a feeling without immediately escaping it
targets.candidate_contributors: Permission for the feeling to occur; distinction between feeling and required action; reduced evaluation of the feeling as a failure; tolerable contact with it.
targets.conditions: Acceptance is neither endorsement of a harmful situation nor a requirement to endure every experience.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Reappraisal
targets.definition: Reappraisal: changing an interpretation in a way that alters emotional response
targets.candidate_contributors: A credible alternative meaning; new contextual information; changed attribution; a different comparison or timescale.
targets.conditions: Reappraisal can alter felt response in studied conditions [S17]; an implausible reinterpretation need not be usable.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Expression control
targets.definition: Expression control: changing whether and how an emotion is displayed
targets.candidate_contributors: Deliberate changes in facial, verbal, or bodily expression; social display rules; a chosen communication purpose.
targets.conditions: Suppressing expression need not reduce feeling and can have different physiological consequences [S17].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Attention regulation
targets.definition: Attention regulation: changing which emotional material receives continued attention
targets.candidate_contributors: Shifting toward or away from evocative details; limiting repeated cues; returning to the current task; deliberately examining an unresolved emotional issue.
targets.conditions: Distraction may provide temporary room without resolving the concern; repeated focus can clarify or prolong it.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Situation selection
targets.definition: Situation selection: changing encounters to alter likely emotional experience
targets.candidate_contributors: Entering, leaving, or changing an encounter; adjusting audience, timing, or exposure; choosing a setting compatible with current needs.
targets.conditions: Avoiding every difficult encounter can also remove valued opportunities; relevance depends on the actual consequence.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Response interruption
targets.definition: Response interruption: interrupting an established emotional reaction
targets.candidate_contributors: Recognizing the early response cue; pausing the next action; changing posture, location, or conversational move; introducing a previously unavailable alternative.
targets.conditions: Interrupting the behavioral sequence does not establish that the emotion has ended.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Co-regulation
targets.definition: Co-regulation: an interaction changing the course of another's emotional state
targets.candidate_contributors: Attentive listening; responsive acknowledgment; practical protection or assistance; pacing that fits the person; shared interpretation of the event.
targets.conditions: Being heard had context-dependent effects in intergroup studies [S21]; intended comfort does not establish actual comfort.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Regulation flexibility
targets.definition: Regulation flexibility: becoming able to use a different response when the familiar one is unhelpful
targets.candidate_contributors: A repertoire of distinct regulation operations; recognition of what the current operation changes; access to another response when conditions differ.
targets.conditions: Flexibility requires relevant selection, not continual switching or a claim that one strategy is always best.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Agency experience
targets.definition: Agency experience: changing the sense of originating or directing an action
targets.candidate_contributors: Correspondence between intention, action, and observed consequence; a meaningful choice; feedback identifying one's contribution; control over execution.
targets.conditions: Felt authorship and actual causal influence can diverge.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Perceived control
targets.definition: Perceived control: changing what one experiences as influenceable
targets.candidate_contributors: An action whose effects are visible; information about genuine limits; reliable access to tools, resources, or authority; removal of arbitrary constraints.
targets.conditions: Control over one variable does not imply control over the whole outcome.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Self-efficacy
targets.definition: Self-efficacy: changing confidence in performing a particular activity
targets.candidate_contributors: Successful performance of the relevant operation; observing a comparable capable actor; specific corrective information; an attainable next challenge.
targets.conditions: Mastery-based and vicarious interventions differed in a particular fear-related study [S19]; generic praise does not establish capability.
