targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Helplessness
targets.definition: Helplessness: changing the expectation or experience that one's action makes no difference
targets.candidate_contributors: Repeated action-outcome independence; obstructed access to effective responses; discovery and use of an action that makes a consequential difference.
targets.conditions: Being told one has control is insufficient when the actual environment remains uncontrollable.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Authorship
targets.definition: Authorship: changing ownership of a choice or contribution
targets.candidate_contributors: Making one's contribution identifiable; real discretion over a choice; acknowledgment of who created which part; separating assistance from substitution.
targets.conditions: Receiving credit and experiencing ownership need not correspond to actual authorship.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Initiation authority
targets.definition: Initiation authority: becoming more or less willing to act without external prompting
targets.candidate_contributors: Clear authority; an unambiguous starting condition; scope for independent choice; prior experience acting without punishment or unnecessary permission.
targets.conditions: Some actions require genuine coordination or authorization; initiative must fit that scope.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Responsibility acceptance
targets.definition: Responsibility acceptance: taking up or relinquishing responsibility appropriately or inappropriately
targets.candidate_contributors: A clear duty or voluntarily adopted commitment; understanding consequences; adequate control and resources; correction of misplaced blame.
targets.conditions: Taking responsibility for an uncontrollable outcome can reduce rather than increase effective agency.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Choice recognition
targets.definition: Choice recognition: becoming aware of alternatives where none seemed available
targets.candidate_contributors: Exposing overlooked feasible actions; removing a false necessity; distinguishing means from ends; identifying a reversible intermediate step.
targets.conditions: A nominal option is not usable if material, social, or cognitive conditions prohibit it.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Dependency recognition
targets.definition: Dependency recognition: identifying which assistance is necessary and which has become habitual
targets.candidate_contributors: Tracing which operation assistance actually supplies; attempting independent components; distinguishing missing capability from familiar delegation.
targets.conditions: Independence is not always beneficial; necessary support can be part of a capable system.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Permission to consider
targets.definition: Permission to consider: allowing an idea to enter examination
targets.candidate_contributors: Separating examination from endorsement; a provisional frame; permission to preserve current commitments during comparison; reduced penalty for entertaining an idea.
targets.conditions: Considering a possibility does not require accepting its truth or desirability.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Permission to disagree
targets.definition: Permission to disagree: becoming able to oppose a claim or authority
targets.candidate_contributors: Recognizing a defensible conflicting judgment; an available expression of it; explicit room for dissent; reduced threat of retaliation.
targets.conditions: Verbal permission alone may be ineffective where actual power consequences remain.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Permission to attempt
targets.definition: Permission to attempt: becoming willing to try without assured success
targets.candidate_contributors: A bounded attempt; a recoverable failure; an attainable first action; separation of trying from promising success.
targets.conditions: Permission cannot supply missing resources or erase genuine consequences.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Permission to stop
targets.definition: Permission to stop: becoming able to end an activity or commitment
targets.candidate_contributors: A legitimate ending criterion; recognition of sunk costs; release from an unnecessary obligation; a preserved route for later return.
targets.conditions: Stopping one method need not abandon the concern it was intended to serve.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Permission to revise
targets.definition: Permission to revise: allowing an earlier position to be replaced
targets.candidate_contributors: A specific reason for revision; separation of accuracy from personal worth; preserving valid prior work; social acceptance of warranted correction.
targets.conditions: Allowing revision is distinct from establishing which replacement is better.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Expression inhibition
targets.definition: Expression inhibition: becoming more or less able to speak or show a response
targets.candidate_contributors: An available phrase or expressive movement; changes in anticipated evaluation; a chosen display rule; a private or supportive setting.
targets.conditions: Silence may reflect deliberate judgment rather than inability or fear.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Impulse inhibition
targets.definition: Impulse inhibition: changing the ability to withhold an immediately available action
targets.candidate_contributors: An early stop cue; time before execution; removal of a triggering opportunity; an alternative response linked to the same cue.
targets.conditions: Withholding one action is easier to specify than suppressing every associated thought or feeling.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Internal prohibition
targets.definition: Internal prohibition: acquiring, relaxing, or rejecting a self-imposed restriction
targets.candidate_contributors: A rule's stated basis; an exception revealing overbreadth; changes in values or circumstances; explicit permission conditioned on consequences.
targets.conditions: Rejecting a restriction without identifying its original function can remove needed protection or coordination.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Social inhibition
targets.definition: Social inhibition: changing restraint associated with anticipated evaluation
targets.candidate_contributors: Actual audience response; anonymity or privacy; familiarity with the setting; clear participation norms; reduced evaluative ambiguity.
targets.conditions: Anticipated judgment may be inaccurate, but real social risk cannot be wished away.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Deliberate restraint
targets.definition: Deliberate restraint: choosing to withhold an action while preserving the ability to perform it
targets.candidate_contributors: A reason to defer; a selected later condition for action; control over timing; an alternative serving the same concern.
targets.conditions: Restraint preserves the available action; inability to act is a different state.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Goal formation
targets.definition: Goal formation: adopting an outcome to pursue
targets.candidate_contributors: A valued possible outcome; an explicit adoption decision; a credible connection to an existing concern; circumstances making pursuit worthwhile.
targets.conditions: Desiring an outcome and committing to organize activity around it are distinct.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Goal abandonment
targets.definition: Goal abandonment: ceasing to pursue a prior outcome
targets.candidate_contributors: Loss of relevance; infeasibility; excessive opportunity cost; a superior way to serve the underlying concern; changed commitments.
targets.conditions: Abandoning a means should not accidentally discard an independently valued end.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Goal priority
targets.definition: Goal priority: changing the order among competing goals
targets.candidate_contributors: Consequences of delay or conflict; prerequisite relationships; scarce resources; explicit precedence among commitments.
targets.conditions: Ranking goals abstractly may fail to resolve the particular next allocation.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Goal specification
targets.definition: Goal specification: making a vague target more determinate
targets.candidate_contributors: Concrete achievement cases; observable completion conditions; scope, beneficiary, and timeframe; a case that looks successful while missing the purpose.
targets.conditions: A measurable substitute can make specification easier while changing the actual goal.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Goal broadening
targets.definition: Goal broadening: recognizing a more encompassing concern
targets.candidate_contributors: Identifying the concern served by several narrower aims; including neglected beneficiaries or downstream consequences.
targets.conditions: A broader goal needs a usable relation to decisions; breadth alone can dissolve actionable distinctions.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Goal substitution
targets.definition: Goal substitution: adopting a different way of expressing the concern
targets.candidate_contributors: An alternative aim serving the same concern; a changed means-end relation; discovery that the original formulation excludes a better route.
targets.conditions: Preserve which end remains stable and which commitment actually changed.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Means-end distinction
targets.definition: Means-end distinction: recognizing that an apparent goal serves another purpose
targets.candidate_contributors: Asking what achieving the apparent goal enables; varying the means while retaining the consequence; a case where the means succeeds but the purpose fails.
targets.conditions: A means can also have intrinsic value; the distinction need not eliminate either role.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Intention formation
targets.definition: Intention formation: resolving to perform an action
targets.candidate_contributors: Selecting a specific act; resolving incompatible choices; accepting its relevant consequences; making the act sufficiently determinate to initiate.
targets.conditions: An intention can remain inactive when its start cue or required capability is absent.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Conditional intention
targets.definition: Conditional intention: relating an intended action to a relevant condition
targets.candidate_contributors: Linking a recognizable condition to a feasible action; rehearsing their connection; specifying exceptions or a fallback.
targets.conditions: Cue-action planning has scoped support [S15]; vague conditions and impossible actions leave the link unusable.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Commitment strength
targets.definition: Commitment strength: changing how strongly a goal governs subsequent activity
targets.candidate_contributors: Protecting time or resources; explicit precedence; repeated enactment; accountability to an accepted commitment; changed reasons for pursuing it.
targets.conditions: Stronger commitment can preserve an obsolete goal; revision conditions still matter.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Option recognition
targets.definition: Option recognition: becoming aware of an existing alternative
targets.candidate_contributors: Information about an overlooked route; a visible available resource; a contrast exposing a false binary; knowledge of an existing alternative.
targets.conditions: Existing in principle and accessible to this actor are different conditions.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Option construction
targets.definition: Option construction: creating an alternative that was previously unavailable
targets.candidate_contributors: Combining available actions or resources; negotiating a new arrangement; changing a constraint; creating an intermediate or reversible option.
targets.conditions: A described alternative becomes available only when its required construction can actually occur.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Criterion selection
targets.definition: Criterion selection: changing what is used to compare options
targets.candidate_contributors: The purpose of the choice; consequences for affected concerns; a failure case under the old criterion; explicit requirements.
targets.conditions: Ease of measurement does not justify choosing the measured property as the governing criterion.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Criterion weighting
targets.definition: Criterion weighting: changing how competing considerations affect a choice
targets.candidate_contributors: Concrete trade-offs; consequences at relevant scales; a priority rule; evidence that a weight changes the selected option.
targets.conditions: Numerical weights can conceal incomparable concerns; retain conflicts that lack an agreed conversion.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Dominance recognition
targets.definition: Dominance recognition: recognizing that one option is no worse on relevant dimensions and better on at least one
targets.candidate_contributors: Aligned dimensions and baselines; comparison of each option on every relevant criterion; justified treatment of uncertainty.
targets.conditions: Dominance applies only over included relevant dimensions; an omitted cost can reverse the result.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Decision threshold
targets.definition: Decision threshold: changing what is sufficient to choose
targets.candidate_contributors: Cost of delay; consequences of error; reversibility; adequacy requirements; expected value of further information.
targets.conditions: A threshold suitable for a reversible action may be inadequate for a consequential commitment.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Choice
targets.definition: Choice: resolving among currently considered alternatives
targets.candidate_contributors: Sufficient differentiation among options; an operative criterion; resolution of relevant conflicts; authority to commit.
targets.conditions: Making a choice does not prove it uniquely best or remove uncertainty about outcomes.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Deferral
targets.definition: Deferral: deciding to preserve an unresolved choice
targets.candidate_contributors: Unresolved consequential information; a valuable later observation; an available temporary arrangement; manageable delay cost.
targets.conditions: Deferral is itself an allocation with consequences; preserve the condition that will reopen the choice.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Reversal
targets.definition: Reversal: replacing a prior choice
targets.candidate_contributors: New evidence; changed circumstances or criteria; a revealed error; an alternative whose gain exceeds switching costs.
targets.conditions: Regret alone does not establish that reversal now improves the outcome.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Contingent choice
targets.definition: Contingent choice: making the selected action depend on a later condition
targets.candidate_contributors: An observable future condition; a preselected feasible action for each relevant branch; preservation of the conditional commitment.
targets.conditions: The future signal must arrive in time and discriminate the branches that matter.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Route construction
targets.definition: Route construction: becoming able to represent a path toward a target
targets.candidate_contributors: Working backward from the target; identifying operations that change required conditions; connecting outputs to later inputs; finding an available first step.
targets.conditions: A sequence of plausible activities is not a route unless its dependencies connect to the target.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Dependency ordering
targets.definition: Dependency ordering: placing prerequisite activities before their consumers
targets.candidate_contributors: Explicit input requirements; lead times; shared resources; identification of operations that cannot start before another completes.
targets.conditions: A visually tidy order can still violate a hidden prerequisite.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Decomposition
targets.definition: Decomposition: dividing an activity into workable contributions
targets.candidate_contributors: Separating contributions by result; locating interfaces; matching subtasks to usable capability; preserving how their results combine.
targets.conditions: Breaking work into smaller pieces can add coordination cost or lose a relation spanning the pieces.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Coordination
targets.definition: Coordination: arranging activities so they support rather than obstruct one another
targets.candidate_contributors: Compatible timing; assigned ownership; shared interface meanings; resource conflict resolution; visibility of mutual dependencies.
targets.conditions: Locally efficient activities can obstruct one another when their outputs or schedules conflict.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Contingency construction
targets.definition: Contingency construction: preparing different continuations for different conditions
targets.candidate_contributors: Consequential alternative conditions; discriminating indicators; feasible responses; a fallback for an unanticipated state.
targets.conditions: Contingencies need resources and authority, not merely labels for possible failures.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Resource preparation
targets.definition: Resource preparation: recognizing and arranging what must be available
targets.candidate_contributors: Inventorying required materials, knowledge, access, time, and collaborators; acquiring or staging missing inputs; reserving constrained resources.
targets.conditions: A listed resource contributes only when available in the needed form at the point of use.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Pacing
targets.definition: Pacing: changing when and how quickly activity proceeds
targets.candidate_contributors: Task demand; time windows; feedback delay; fatigue and recovery; dependencies on others' timing.
targets.conditions: Faster local execution can create downstream waiting, rework, or overload.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Monitoring plan
targets.definition: Monitoring plan: deciding what observations should change the plan
targets.candidate_contributors: Identifying observations that discriminate success, failure, or changed conditions; defining what each observation should alter.
targets.conditions: Monitoring without a connected decision can consume effort without changing the plan.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Resumption preparation
targets.definition: Resumption preparation: making an interrupted activity easier to resume
targets.candidate_contributors: Recording current state, unfinished dependencies, and next action; preserving materials; setting a relevant return cue.
targets.conditions: A vague note such as 'continue project' may omit the context needed to resume.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Initiation
targets.definition: Initiation: beginning an intended or triggered activity
targets.candidate_contributors: A detected start condition; an executable first action; available materials and authority; removal of immediate friction; a learned trigger.
targets.conditions: Stronger intention cannot initiate an action whose first operation remains unspecified or inaccessible.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Cessation
targets.definition: Cessation: ending an ongoing activity
targets.candidate_contributors: A recognized completion or stop condition; a competing priority; an interruption mechanism; release from a sustaining cue.
targets.conditions: Stopping behavior and stopping its mental rehearsal are separate effects.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Switching
targets.definition: Switching: changing from one activity to another
targets.candidate_contributors: A selected incoming activity; preservation of outgoing state; an explicit transition; availability of the incoming task's requirements.
targets.conditions: Unfinished previous instructions can interfere with the new activity.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Sequencing
targets.definition: Sequencing: executing components in a different order
targets.candidate_contributors: A learned sequence; external ordering cues; prerequisite information; correction of a mistaken transition.
targets.conditions: Execution order must track task dependencies rather than mere familiarity.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Speed control
targets.definition: Speed control: accelerating or slowing an operation
targets.candidate_contributors: Time constraints; simpler operations; practiced components; reduced decision overhead; deliberate pacing.
targets.conditions: Speed can trade against accuracy or coordination; specify which errors and delays matter.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Precision control
targets.definition: Precision control: changing the care or accuracy applied
targets.candidate_contributors: A more discriminating target; better sensory or informational feedback; slower or decomposed execution where useful; correction of a recurrent error.
targets.conditions: Extra care cannot repair an inaccurate standard or an unavailable measurement.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Online correction
targets.definition: Online correction: adjusting an action while it is underway
targets.candidate_contributors: Timely information about deviation; a valid desired state; an available adjustment; control over the relevant action variable.
targets.conditions: Feedback arriving after the irreversible step cannot support correction of that step.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Resumption
targets.definition: Resumption: returning to an interrupted activity
targets.candidate_contributors: A preserved task-state record; a distinctive return cue; recovery of the next dependency; reconstruction of the interrupted context.
targets.conditions: Remembering the general goal may leave the exact restart operation unavailable.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Completion
targets.definition: Completion: bringing an activity to its appropriate ending
targets.candidate_contributors: A concrete completion condition; recognition that it is met; delivery to the required consumer; closure of necessary loose ends.
targets.conditions: Stopping because effort is exhausted does not establish completion; unnecessary polishing can prevent an adequate ending.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Interruptibility
targets.definition: Interruptibility: remaining able to stop or redirect an otherwise ongoing process
targets.candidate_contributors: Accessible stop or redirect signals; periodic points for checking conditions; retained control over execution; absence of blocking commitments.
targets.conditions: A stop rule is ineffective if the running process cannot receive or obey it.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Persistence
targets.definition: Persistence: continuing despite an obstacle or delay
targets.candidate_contributors: A still-valued attainable outcome; visible progress; an alternative around the obstacle; sufficient resources; a reason the delay is worth bearing.
targets.conditions: Persistence is beneficial only while the continuation retains a credible contribution.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Disengagement
targets.definition: Disengagement: withdrawing effort from an activity
targets.candidate_contributors: Recognition of poor prospects or changed relevance; excessive cost; an available alternative; permission to release the commitment.
targets.conditions: Disengaging from an ineffective method can preserve effort for the original purpose.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Frustration tolerance
targets.definition: Frustration tolerance: remaining able to proceed while frustrated
targets.candidate_contributors: A usable next action despite the obstruction; separating discomfort from impossibility; interpreting the setback accurately; room to pause without losing progress.
targets.conditions: Tolerance does not require enduring a preventable obstruction indefinitely.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Effort allocation
targets.definition: Effort allocation: changing how much effort an activity receives
targets.candidate_contributors: Expected contribution of additional effort; remaining difficulty; deadlines; available energy; an explicit allocation decision.
targets.conditions: Effort amount is a poor proxy when the selected operation cannot supply the missing result.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Effort distribution
targets.definition: Effort distribution: changing how effort is divided across activities
targets.candidate_contributors: Comparison of activities' marginal contributions; shared bottlenecks; dependency order; protected resources for neglected prerequisites.
targets.conditions: Evenly distributing effort can leave a critical dependency under-resourced.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Recovery pacing
targets.definition: Recovery pacing: changing the relation between exertion and restoration
targets.candidate_contributors: Recognition of declining function; task-specific restoration needs; breaks at workable boundaries; reduced accumulation of unresolved demands.
targets.conditions: Feeling rested and restored performance may differ; recovery requirements vary with the demand [S01].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Delay endurance
targets.definition: Delay endurance: remaining engaged without immediate reward
targets.candidate_contributors: Credible later value; visible intermediate progress; meaningful activity during waiting; protection against competing immediate demands.
targets.conditions: Enduring delay is unhelpful when the promised outcome is no longer plausible or valuable.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Adaptive stopping
targets.definition: Adaptive stopping: ceasing when further effort no longer serves the concern
targets.candidate_contributors: A completion criterion; evidence that further effort adds little; changed alternatives; costs exceeding the remaining contribution.
targets.conditions: Stopping needs the actual purpose as reference, not merely fatigue or an arbitrary iteration count.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Re-engagement
targets.definition: Re-engagement: recovering willingness to return after a setback
targets.candidate_contributors: A revised feasible route; corrected explanation of the setback; preserved prior progress; an attainable restart action.
targets.conditions: Repeating encouragement without changing the failed dependency can reproduce the setback.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Habit acquisition
targets.definition: Habit acquisition: a response becoming more reliably triggered by a recurring condition
targets.candidate_contributors: Repeated performance in a recurring context; a stable recognizable cue; low initiation friction; repeated consequences that maintain the response.
targets.conditions: Daily-life automaticity varied substantially between people and behaviors; repetition is not a fixed-duration guarantee [S16].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Habit weakening
targets.definition: Habit weakening: a previously recurrent response becoming less automatic
targets.candidate_contributors: Reduced contact with the old cue; interruption of its usual response; altered context; an alternative response becoming available.
targets.conditions: Temporary nonperformance need not erase the cue-response tendency; it can return in a familiar context.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Cue reassignment
targets.definition: Cue reassignment: changing which condition activates a response
targets.candidate_contributors: Repeated pairing of the intended response with a new cue; distinct separation from the old cue; a cue available at the right time.
targets.conditions: Similar cues may continue to trigger the old response unless their relevant difference is learned.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Routine replacement
targets.definition: Routine replacement: one familiar response giving way to another
targets.candidate_contributors: A replacement that serves the old routine's function; an accessible response at the same trigger; altered reward or friction; repeated enactment.
targets.conditions: Removing the old routine without supplying its useful function can leave a recurring unmet need.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Automatic initiation
targets.definition: Automatic initiation: beginning without a fresh explicit decision
targets.candidate_contributors: A well-learned start cue; preparation of the first action; stable access to materials; minimal need for a fresh choice.
targets.conditions: Automatic starting can occur after the original goal has ceased to apply.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Automatic sequencing
targets.definition: Automatic sequencing: a learned sequence proceeding with less stepwise direction
targets.candidate_contributors: Repeated ordered transitions; reliable feedback between steps; grouping components into a practiced unit.
targets.conditions: A fluent sequence can preserve an obsolete or incorrect step.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: De-automation
targets.definition: De-automation: bringing a familiar routine back under deliberate examination
targets.candidate_contributors: A pause at the relevant step; explicit inspection of the routine's conditions; a novel case that breaks habitual execution.
targets.conditions: Awareness of a routine does not immediately provide an alternative method.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Context discrimination
targets.definition: Context discrimination: a routine becoming restricted to appropriate conditions
targets.candidate_contributors: Contrasting contexts requiring and forbidding the routine; distinctive relevance cues; exceptions encountered during use.
targets.conditions: A routine learned in one setting may transfer too broadly or fail to activate elsewhere.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Automatic interruption
targets.definition: Automatic interruption: a learned stopping condition interrupting a routine
targets.candidate_contributors: A salient stop condition; repeated cue-stop pairing; an available interrupt action; preserved detection during the routine.
targets.conditions: The stop signal must remain accessible while execution consumes attention.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Skill acquisition
targets.definition: Skill acquisition: becoming able to perform a previously unavailable operation
targets.candidate_contributors: A demonstrable operation; required prerequisite abilities; performance on a manageable instance; information about the failed component; further use that incorporates the correction.
targets.conditions: Instruction can supply a procedure while leaving a sensory, motor, social, or resource dependency unresolved.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Fluency
targets.definition: Fluency: performing with less hesitation
targets.candidate_contributors: Familiarity with valid transitions; retrieval of needed components; removal of repeated decision points; coordinated practice.
targets.conditions: Reduced hesitation can reflect confidence rather than improved competence.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Accuracy
targets.definition: Accuracy: making fewer or more consequential errors
targets.candidate_contributors: A correct target standard; discrimination of near errors; precise information about deviations; repair of the error-producing operation.
targets.conditions: A higher success rate on easier cases may conceal unchanged accuracy on the required task.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Speed
targets.definition: Speed: performing an operation more quickly or slowly
targets.candidate_contributors: More efficient operations; automatic retrieval of practiced components; reduced unnecessary movement or switching; advance preparation.
targets.conditions: A speed gain is scoped to the operation and conditions; preserve consequential accuracy requirements.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Coordination
targets.definition: Coordination: combining components into an effective activity
targets.candidate_contributors: Compatible component timing; stable interfaces; practice of transitions; feedback about the combined result.
targets.conditions: Competence in each component separately does not establish competence in their joint execution.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Discrimination skill
targets.definition: Discrimination skill: recognizing distinctions needed for competent performance
targets.candidate_contributors: Examples differing on the performance-critical feature; attention to that feature; corrective information; practice with near neighbors.
targets.conditions: Discrimination learned from superficial cues can fail when those cues change.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Adaptation
targets.definition: Adaptation: modifying a skill for altered conditions
targets.candidate_contributors: Information about a changed condition; a model of what the skill depends on; altered action parameters; experience of the resulting error.
targets.conditions: Adaptation to a particular motor environment does not establish general flexibility; transfer depends on the learned representation [S26].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Transfer
targets.definition: Transfer: using a capability in a different setting
targets.candidate_contributors: Correspondence between old and new task relations; varied examples; explicit application conditions; performance in the receiving setting.
targets.conditions: Transfer across negotiation cases benefited from supported comparison [S09]; distant transfer remains a separate question.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Retention
targets.definition: Retention: preserving a capability over time
targets.candidate_contributors: Later retrieval or execution; distributed encounters; preserved application cues; reconstruction after disuse.
targets.conditions: Fact-learning experiments link useful spacing to the retention interval [S25]; retention of a particular skill needs its own evidence.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Skill loss and recovery
targets.definition: Skill loss and recovery: losing or recovering a previously available capability
targets.candidate_contributors: Disuse, interference, or changed bodily conditions; recovery of missing cues; relearning a lost component; restoration of required support.
targets.conditions: Faster reacquisition does not establish that every component remained available throughout the loss.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Example learning
targets.definition: Example learning: retaining something from a particular case
targets.candidate_contributors: Attention to the case's relevant structure; an accurate record; relating its outcome to its conditions; retrieving it when a similar relation matters.
targets.conditions: Remembering an anecdote does not establish its representativeness or its causal explanation.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Rule learning
targets.definition: Rule learning: acquiring a relation that applies across cases
targets.candidate_contributors: Comparison across varied cases; detection of an invariant relation; explicit contrasting nonexamples; use of the rule on a new case.
targets.conditions: A rule fitting the presented cases may still depend on an unvaried incidental feature.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Association learning
targets.definition: Association learning: changing the relation between a cue and another event
targets.candidate_contributors: Predictive co-occurrence between cue and event; changes in their contingency; repeated violation of an old prediction; distinctive context.
targets.conditions: The association's strength and its conscious verbal description may change differently.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Outcome learning
targets.definition: Outcome learning: changing future conduct in light of consequences
targets.candidate_contributors: Consequences linked clearly to a particular action; information about alternatives; an updated expectation that influences the next relevant choice.
targets.conditions: Delayed or ambiguous consequences can be attributed to the wrong action.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Discrimination learning
targets.definition: Discrimination learning: learning when superficially similar cases require different responses
targets.candidate_contributors: Contrasting cases that look alike but require different responses; a diagnostic feature; corrective experience at the confusion point.
targets.conditions: The distinguishing cue must remain available under actual performance conditions.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Generalization
targets.definition: Generalization: extending a learned relation to further cases
targets.candidate_contributors: Shared operative structure; varied instances; abstraction of the relevant relationship; a new case that satisfies its conditions.
targets.conditions: Generalization can extend an error as readily as a useful relation.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Generalization restriction
targets.definition: Generalization restriction: preventing transfer where the relation does not hold
targets.candidate_contributors: Boundary cases; explicit exclusions; contrast between superficial resemblance and a missing precondition; a retrieval cue for the exception.
targets.conditions: Listing exceptions separately is insufficient if they are absent when the rule is applied.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Interference change
targets.definition: Interference change: one learning experience helping or obstructing another
targets.candidate_contributors: Similarity between competing material; timing and context of acquisition; shared useful structure; separation of incompatible rules.
targets.conditions: Earlier learning can facilitate or interfere depending on what carries over.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Relearning
targets.definition: Relearning: reacquiring something previously learned
targets.candidate_contributors: Residual cues and components; re-exposure to the governing relation; practice focused on the unavailable step; recovery of original context.
targets.conditions: A returning feeling of familiarity does not establish full reacquisition.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Learning-strategy change
targets.definition: Learning-strategy change: altering how one acquires or retains a capability
targets.candidate_contributors: Evidence about what a method makes available later; identifying the current learning dependency; adopting retrieval, comparison, demonstration, or another fitting operation.
targets.conditions: A strategy that improves immediate ease may worsen later retention [S06].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Knowledge monitoring
targets.definition: Knowledge monitoring: recognizing what one knows and does not know
targets.candidate_contributors: Attempted retrieval; source and scope checks; a question requiring the allegedly known information; comparison with an authoritative record.
targets.conditions: Failure to retrieve can reflect access difficulty rather than absent learning; successful guessing can mislead too.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Comprehension monitoring
targets.definition: Comprehension monitoring: distinguishing understanding from familiarity with wording
targets.candidate_contributors: Explaining the mechanism; deriving a consequence; applying it to a new case; locating missing dependencies.
targets.conditions: Self-rated understanding may fall after explanatory demands expose gaps [S14]; an exposed gap still needs repair.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Error detection
targets.definition: Error detection: noticing a mistake in one's own activity
targets.candidate_contributors: A discrepancy between intended and observed result; an invariant check; a counterexample; an independently constructed comparison.
targets.conditions: Repeated inspection using the same mistaken assumption can miss the same error.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Assumption detection
targets.definition: Assumption detection: recognizing an unexamined starting commitment
targets.candidate_contributors: Making premises explicit; varying a supposedly fixed condition; asking what a conclusion requires; a case where the starting commitment fails.
targets.conditions: An assumption can be useful when openly provisional; detection does not require immediate rejection.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Conflict detection
targets.definition: Conflict detection: recognizing incompatible demands or interpretations
targets.candidate_contributors: Making competing demands simultaneously available; aligning their scope; constructing a case where they prescribe incompatible continuations.
targets.conditions: Conflicting wording can be resolved by interpretation, while conflicting requirements may need a substantive choice.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Method applicability
targets.definition: Method applicability: recognizing whether a procedure fits the present matter
targets.candidate_contributors: Comparing required inputs and exclusions with the live case; an applicable and inapplicable example; inspection of the method's actual output.
targets.conditions: A familiar method's name or subject area does not establish applicability.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Mental-state recognition
targets.definition: Mental-state recognition: noticing that fatigue, emotion, or attention is affecting activity
targets.candidate_contributors: A change in performance or experience; an independent state cue; comparison across conditions; specific recognition of distraction or fatigue.
targets.conditions: Subjective adaptation can conceal performance impairment; one feeling is not a complete state measure [S01].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Confidence monitoring
targets.definition: Confidence monitoring: noticing mismatch between certainty and support
targets.candidate_contributors: A confident claim with weak grounds; a low-confidence answer with strong evidence; resolved predictions; separation of familiarity from support.
targets.conditions: Monitoring a mismatch is different from correcting the cue that produced it.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Limitation localization
targets.definition: Limitation localization: identifying the particular operation that is unavailable
targets.candidate_contributors: Tracing failure to a missing distinction, input, operation, resource, or interface; preserving components that still work.
targets.conditions: A global label such as 'bad reasoning' does not locate an actionable limitation.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Self-correction
targets.definition: Self-correction: changing one's activity in response to a recognized inadequacy
targets.candidate_contributors: A recognized error connected to a replacement operation; revision of dependent work; later access to the correction at its trigger.
targets.conditions: An acknowledgment without changed applicable conduct leaves correction uptake unestablished.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Approach selection
targets.definition: Approach selection: adopting a different way of proceeding
targets.candidate_contributors: The missing contribution; available methods with explicit outputs; a separating comparison; a new condition defeating the old approach.
targets.conditions: Choosing a method and obtaining its promised result are separate events.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Approach construction
targets.definition: Approach construction: creating a method absent from the repertoire
targets.candidate_contributors: Decomposing the required result into operations; composing available capabilities; defining previously unspecified transitions; constructing a usable interface.
targets.conditions: A description can hide unavailable suboperations; construction must expose those dependencies.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Question order
targets.definition: Question order: changing which determination is made first
targets.candidate_contributors: Actual prerequisites among determinations; availability of discriminating information; the cost of resolving a question too early.
targets.conditions: A fixed universal question order can obstruct tasks whose useful entry point differs.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Depth
targets.definition: Depth: pursuing a relationship further before proceeding
targets.candidate_contributors: An unresolved consequential relation; a missing intermediate step; an explanation still relying on an unexamined dependency.
targets.conditions: Additional depth helps only while it changes what the activity can establish or do.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Breadth
targets.definition: Breadth: considering a wider range of matters or alternatives
targets.candidate_contributors: An excluded relevant domain; alternative mechanisms or formulations; variation in consequential dimensions; discovery of omitted cases.
targets.conditions: Wider enumeration can add duplicates without improving coverage.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Explicitness
targets.definition: Explicitness: bringing an implicit operation into inspectable form
targets.candidate_contributors: Externalizing intermediate results, assumptions, selection criteria, or transformations; identifying the consumer of each.
targets.conditions: Inspectability can improve without the underlying operation becoming correct.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Provisionality
targets.definition: Provisionality: separating temporary use from settled reliance
targets.candidate_contributors: Explicit status labels; preserving alternative accounts; limiting use to the assumed scope; a trigger for reconsideration.
targets.conditions: A provisional premise must retain its status in downstream conclusions and later reuse.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Burden of justification
targets.definition: Burden of justification: changing what must be established before accepting or excluding something
targets.candidate_contributors: Consequences of acceptance or exclusion; asymmetry of error; available support; the scope and strength of the claim.
targets.conditions: Excessive demands can exclude useful justified possibilities; weak demands can admit unsupported ones.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Stopping rule
targets.definition: Stopping rule: changing what warrants ending inquiry
targets.candidate_contributors: Completion conditions tied to the actual use; remaining consequential uncertainty; additional inquiry cost; a warranted continuation outside the current scope.
targets.conditions: Stopping inquiry is not equivalent to declaring every parent question resolved.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Perspective replacement
targets.definition: Perspective replacement: changing the interpretation governing the activity
targets.candidate_contributors: A representation exposing an important omission; a better-supported interpretation; a changed target or criterion; reconstruction of dependent operations.
targets.conditions: New language alone leaves the governing perspective unchanged if it selects the same inadequate continuation.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Self-description
targets.definition: Self-description: changing the traits or capacities attributed to oneself
targets.candidate_contributors: Evidence from one's actions; feedback from relevant others; new roles or capacities; comparison across contexts; revised interpretation of prior events.
targets.conditions: A single episode may change self-description without establishing an enduring trait.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Role identity
targets.definition: Role identity: taking up, revising, or leaving an understood role
targets.candidate_contributors: Taking on or leaving responsibilities; social recognition; repeated enactment; changed expectations; a new account of what the role requires.
targets.conditions: A title alone need not alter operative identity or actual responsibility.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Group identification
targets.definition: Group identification: changing which groups are included in one's self-understanding
targets.candidate_contributors: Shared activity and commitments; acceptance or exclusion; perceived similarity; group narratives; changed relations to other affiliations.
targets.conditions: Identification can vary by situation and need not imply agreement with every group norm.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Self-worth
targets.definition: Self-worth: changing one's evaluation of oneself
targets.candidate_contributors: Experienced acceptance or rejection; self-evaluation standards; interpretation of success and failure; separation of specific performance from global worth.
targets.conditions: Praise can be unconvincing when it conflicts with experience or rests on an unwanted evaluative standard.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Possible self
targets.definition: Possible self: becoming able to imagine oneself living or acting differently
targets.candidate_contributors: A concrete alternative life or action; a comparable example; an attainable path; opportunities to enact a previously untried role.
targets.conditions: Imagining a possible self does not establish desire, feasibility, or continuity of commitment.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Self-continuity
targets.definition: Self-continuity: changing the perceived connection among past, present, and future self
targets.candidate_contributors: Recognizing continuing concerns or relationships; linking past choices with current circumstances; representing later consequences as one's own.
targets.conditions: Continuity need not mean preserving every old commitment or denying substantial change.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Self-boundary
targets.definition: Self-boundary: changing what is experienced as belonging to oneself
targets.candidate_contributors: Changes in bodily ownership cues; personal responsibility and possession judgments; close identification with roles, relationships, or tools.
targets.conditions: These are different senses of boundary; changes in one do not establish changes in another.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Authenticity
targets.definition: Authenticity: changing the relation between experienced and presented identity
targets.candidate_contributors: Recognizing a mismatch between private commitments and public conduct; room for candid expression; altering a role or presentation.
targets.conditions: Feeling authentic does not establish that one's self-interpretation is accurate or that every impulse should be expressed.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Identity flexibility
targets.definition: Identity flexibility: becoming more or less able to revise a self-description
targets.candidate_contributors: Evidence that a self-description is context-dependent; examples of change; reduced penalties for revising a label; a stable concern surviving the revision.
targets.conditions: Flexibility can coexist with stable commitments; instability is not inherently an improvement.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Label attachment
targets.definition: Label attachment: changing how strongly a label constrains self-interpretation
targets.candidate_contributors: Repeated use of a label; social reinforcement; interpreting new events through it; contrasting cases outside its predictions.
targets.conditions: Removing a label can free interpretation or remove useful recognition; retain consequential distinctions.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Event interpretation
targets.definition: Event interpretation: changing what a past event is understood to mean
targets.candidate_contributors: New evidence about the event; a changed understanding of participants' knowledge or constraints; connection to later consequences; alternative meanings.
targets.conditions: Changed meaning does not establish changed historical facts; preserve observation and reconstruction separately.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Life narrative
targets.definition: Life narrative: reorganizing how events belong to a personal history
targets.candidate_contributors: Selecting different turning points; linking episodes through shared concerns; correcting chronology or causality; integrating previously omitted periods.
targets.conditions: A coherent narrative can misrepresent complexity or uncertainty in the underlying history.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Past responsibility
targets.definition: Past responsibility: revising one's understanding of agency or responsibility in a remembered event
targets.candidate_contributors: Evidence about actual options, knowledge, power, and obligations at the time; correction of hindsight assumptions; distinguishing contribution from total control.
targets.conditions: Current capability should not be projected backward as an available past option.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Past relevance
targets.definition: Past relevance: changing which earlier events are used to understand the present
targets.candidate_contributors: A present situation cueing a prior episode; recognition of a shared relation; differentiation from a superficially similar but irrelevant event.
targets.conditions: A memorable past event may dominate despite weak applicability to the present case.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Continuity recognition
targets.definition: Continuity recognition: finding or losing a connection across life periods
targets.candidate_contributors: Tracing a concern, relationship, or recurring response across periods; locating genuine discontinuities; recovering missing contextual links.
targets.conditions: A constructed connection requires evidence; similarity alone need not imply a continuous cause.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Reconciliation
targets.definition: Reconciliation: becoming able to hold previously conflicting parts of one's history together
targets.candidate_contributors: Distinguishing different contexts and commitments; accepting that multiple interpretations capture different aspects; repairing a factual misunderstanding.
targets.conditions: Holding complexity together need not erase conflict, loss, or responsibility.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Future implication
targets.definition: Future implication: changing what the past is taken to imply about what can happen next
targets.candidate_contributors: Separating a past constraint from a permanent limit; evidence of changed conditions; identifying retained capacities and new routes.
targets.conditions: An encouraging future interpretation must preserve real constraints and uncertainty.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Significance
targets.definition: Significance: something coming to seem meaningful or meaningless
targets.candidate_contributors: Connection to a valued concern; participation in a larger activity or relationship; a newly recognized consequence; loss of an old organizing relation.
targets.conditions: Meaning can change while the immediate task stays identical; the changed relation should be specified.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Purpose formation
targets.definition: Purpose formation: adopting a reason that organizes continuing activity
targets.candidate_contributors: A concern able to organize repeated choices; an adopted contribution or responsibility; concrete occasions for enactment.
targets.conditions: A purpose statement becomes operative only through its relationship to actual allocation and action.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Coherence
targets.definition: Coherence: experiencing matters as fitting together or fragmenting
targets.candidate_contributors: Recognizable relationships among events and commitments; resolution of contradictions; a narrative or model connecting previously fragmented material.
targets.conditions: Felt coherence can increase through an inaccurate simplifying account.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Direction
targets.definition: Direction: gaining or losing a sense of where activity is leading
targets.candidate_contributors: An intelligible next dependency; a credible route from current activity to a valued outcome; visible cumulative progress.
targets.conditions: A detailed schedule may create direction without establishing that the destination is worthwhile.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Contribution meaning
targets.definition: Contribution meaning: recognizing how one's activity matters beyond its immediate performance
targets.candidate_contributors: Seeing who uses the result; observing consequences beyond the task; feedback from beneficiaries; connecting local work to a larger dependency.
targets.conditions: Symbolic recognition and actual contribution can differ; both should remain identifiable.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Existential orientation
targets.definition: Existential orientation: changing one's relation to uncertainty, finitude, or life's possibilities
targets.candidate_contributors: Reflection on uncertainty or finitude; encounters with loss or possibility; philosophical or spiritual interpretations; chosen commitments under unresolved questions.
targets.conditions: No single framing is guaranteed to fit every person's worldview or experience.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Purpose revision
targets.definition: Purpose revision: replacing an organizing commitment that no longer fits
targets.candidate_contributors: A persistent mismatch with lived concerns; changed conditions or capacities; an alternative organizing commitment; permission to release obsolete obligations.
targets.conditions: Replacing purpose can require transition support; a new slogan may leave prior allocation intact.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Present orientation
targets.definition: Present orientation: changing how much current experience dominates
targets.candidate_contributors: Attention to current sensation and action; immediate demands or rewards; reduced future cues; deliberate selection of a present activity.
targets.conditions: Present attention can support contact with experience or conceal a consequential future dependency.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Future horizon
targets.definition: Future horizon: considering a longer or shorter interval ahead
targets.candidate_contributors: Representing delayed consequences; a longer planning interval; credible information about future conditions; including later beneficiaries.
targets.conditions: Longer horizons can add uncertainty and speculation; include distinctions that change present choices.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Past orientation
targets.definition: Past orientation: changing how strongly earlier events organize present attention
targets.candidate_contributors: Recurring reminders; autobiographical interpretation; unresolved past concerns; deliberate retrieval or backgrounding of earlier events.
targets.conditions: Past attention can supply needed learning or displace current information; relevance decides the difference.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Future-self connection
targets.definition: Future-self connection: changing the felt or understood relevance of later consequences to oneself
targets.candidate_contributors: Concrete representation of one's later situation; recognition of continuing interests; contact with foreseeable consequences; future-oriented commitments.
targets.conditions: Age-progressed self-images affected allocation choices in experiments; enduring behavior change is a broader claim [S23].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Subjective duration
targets.definition: Subjective duration: time seeming to pass more quickly or slowly
targets.candidate_contributors: Attention to elapsed time; density of noticed events; arousal; boredom or absorption; how an interval is remembered.
targets.conditions: Duration judged during an interval can differ from duration reconstructed afterward.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Patience
targets.definition: Patience: changing willingness to wait
targets.candidate_contributors: Credible expected benefit of waiting; tolerable present conditions; an activity during the delay; trust in eventual delivery.
targets.conditions: Waiting longer is not beneficial when delay destroys value or the promised result is unreliable.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Urgency calibration
targets.definition: Urgency calibration: changing when haste is experienced as warranted
targets.candidate_contributors: Actual deadline and delay consequences; expiring opportunities; comparison with recoverable delays; removal of artificial pressure.
targets.conditions: A strong feeling of haste does not establish a high cost of waiting.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Temporal possibility
targets.definition: Temporal possibility: seeing that a different sequence or timing changes what can happen
targets.candidate_contributors: Reordering prerequisites; staging resources earlier; exploiting a time window; separating simultaneous demands; deferring a reversible commitment.
targets.conditions: A new sequence changes possibility only through real timing dependencies.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Perspective differentiation
targets.definition: Perspective differentiation: distinguishing another's viewpoint from one's own
targets.candidate_contributors: Separating one's information from the other's; knowledge of their access and aims; direct statements revealing a consequential difference.
targets.conditions: Understanding one's own reaction is insufficient evidence of the other's viewpoint [S12].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Intention interpretation
targets.definition: Intention interpretation: changing what another is understood to be trying to do
targets.candidate_contributors: The person's stated aim; available alternatives; observed choices; surrounding constraints; clarification of ambiguous behavior.
targets.conditions: The same behavior can serve different intentions; retain unresolved accounts where they fit equally well.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Knowledge attribution
targets.definition: Knowledge attribution: revising what another is assumed to know
targets.candidate_contributors: The person's actual explanations and questions; prior exposure; demonstrated use of the relevant information; explicit correction of an assumption.
targets.conditions: Fluent vocabulary or agreement does not establish knowledge of the needed relation.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Emotion recognition
targets.definition: Emotion recognition: changing one's interpretation of another's feelings
targets.candidate_contributors: The person's description; contextual information; verbal and nonverbal signals; changes across the interaction.
targets.conditions: No isolated expression uniquely identifies a feeling; ask only when the missing distinction materially matters.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Empathic understanding
targets.definition: Empathic understanding: becoming more or less able to understand another's experience
targets.candidate_contributors: Receiving the person's account; understanding the events and concerns that organize it; checking the interpretation against their corrections.
targets.conditions: Imagined empathy can misread the person; getting relevant perspective improved accuracy in studied tasks [S12].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Dispositional attribution
targets.definition: Dispositional attribution: changing what traits are attributed to another
targets.candidate_contributors: Repeated behavior across relevant settings; distinction between stable patterns and situational constraint; information contradicting an initial impression.
targets.conditions: A trait label may compress behavior without explaining its mechanism.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Situational understanding
targets.definition: Situational understanding: recognizing how another's circumstances shape their response
targets.candidate_contributors: Information about actual incentives, limitations, relationships, and available knowledge; comparison with how the same actor behaves elsewhere.
targets.conditions: A plausible imagined circumstance is not evidence that it actually applied.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Stereotype revision
targets.definition: Stereotype revision: changing a generalization applied to a group member
targets.candidate_contributors: Diagnostic counterinstances; attention to individual information; a more representative range of cases; revision of overbroad group inferences.
targets.conditions: One salient exception may be treated as exceptional without revising the generalization.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Misunderstanding recognition
targets.definition: Misunderstanding recognition: noticing that one's account of another was inadequate
targets.candidate_contributors: An unexpected response; explicit correction; a prediction contradicted by the person's account; evidence that the inferred state was wrong.
targets.conditions: Recognition must update dependent responses; merely acknowledging the correction leaves the misunderstanding operative.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Source trust
targets.definition: Source trust: changing reliance on a source of information
targets.candidate_contributors: Accuracy and provenance of prior claims; transparent access to evidence; incentives and conflicts; willingness to correct specific errors.
targets.conditions: Credible presentation and evidence-bearing reliability are different contributors to reliance.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Competence trust
targets.definition: Competence trust: changing confidence in another's ability in a specified domain
targets.candidate_contributors: Relevant demonstrated performance; limits openly specified; successful handling of difficult cases; evidence of transfer to the required domain.
targets.conditions: Competence in one task should not automatically extend to another.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Benevolence trust
targets.definition: Benevolence trust: changing expectation that another takes one's interests into account
targets.candidate_contributors: Actions reflecting the person's interests when alternatives were available; responsiveness to stated needs; treatment under conflicting incentives.
targets.conditions: Friendly tone is weak evidence when conduct repeatedly disregards those interests.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Integrity trust
targets.definition: Integrity trust: changing expectation that another acts consistently with stated commitments
targets.candidate_contributors: Correspondence between commitments and later conduct; handling of costly exceptions; truthful correction; consistent application of stated standards.
targets.conditions: Rigid consistency with a mistaken commitment is not the same as justified integrity.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Self-trust
targets.definition: Self-trust: changing willingness to rely on one's own judgment
targets.candidate_contributors: Relevant successful judgment; accurate recognition of limits; repair of a specific error; distinction between a local failure and global incapacity.
targets.conditions: Self-trust should be scoped; confidence alone does not establish reliable judgment.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Trust scope
targets.definition: Trust scope: narrowing or extending where reliance is appropriate
targets.candidate_contributors: Domain-specific performance; changing stakes and conditions; failures revealing a boundary; independent corroboration where transfer is uncertain.
targets.conditions: Trust can remain warranted locally after a failure elsewhere.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Trust repair
targets.definition: Trust repair: restoring some reliance after a breach
targets.candidate_contributors: Acknowledgment of the actual breach; credible correction of its cause; repair of its consequences; subsequent conduct bearing on renewed reliance.
targets.conditions: An apology's persuasive effect does not itself establish that the breach-producing condition changed.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Skepticism
targets.definition: Skepticism: becoming more or less inclined to demand supporting grounds
targets.candidate_contributors: A discovered error; awareness of incentives or missing support; a requirement for independent grounds; a history of reliable evidence.
targets.conditions: Indiscriminate doubt can reject well-supported claims as readily as weak ones.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Deference
targets.definition: Deference: changing whose judgment governs when judgments conflict
