targets.candidate_contributors: Relevant expertise; quality of available reasons; division of responsibility; time or capability limits; an accepted decision procedure.
targets.conditions: Deference can be rational without implying that the deferred-to person is infallible.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Independence
targets.definition: Independence: becoming able to evaluate a claim without relying on a favored source
targets.candidate_contributors: Access to underlying evidence; a usable evaluation method; independent comparison; separation of claim content from source affinity.
targets.conditions: Independence requires capability and information; rejecting authority reflexively is still source-dependent judgment.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Belonging
targets.definition: Belonging: feeling more or less included in a group or relationship
targets.candidate_contributors: Actual invitations and inclusion; recognized contribution; shared activity; reliable access to the group; interpretation of ambiguous social events.
targets.conditions: Feeling included and receiving fair access may diverge; wording alone cannot supply missing participation.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Connection
targets.definition: Connection: experiencing greater or lesser interpersonal closeness
targets.candidate_contributors: Mutual responsiveness; shared attention and activity; appropriate reciprocal disclosure; repeated meaningful interaction.
targets.conditions: Structured disclosure increased short-term closeness relative to small talk in one study; durable closeness is separate [S20].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Alienation
targets.definition: Alienation: feeling more or less estranged
targets.candidate_contributors: Exclusion; unrecognized experience; persistent mismatch with surrounding norms; loss of meaningful participation; renewed opportunity to be heard.
targets.conditions: Being present in a group does not establish connection or acknowledgment.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Respect
targets.definition: Respect: changing one's regard for another's standing or contribution
targets.candidate_contributors: Recognition of a person's standing, effort, competence, or contribution; direct encounter with their work; revised evidence about conduct.
targets.conditions: Respect for standing and admiration of performance need not rise and fall together.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Affection
targets.definition: Affection: changing warmth or fondness
targets.candidate_contributors: Caring encounters; appreciated qualities; positive shared history; responsive attention; changes in trust or repeated hurt.
targets.conditions: Warmth cannot be demanded into existence; outward friendliness may conceal a different feeling.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Hostility
targets.definition: Hostility: changing antagonism or readiness to oppose
targets.candidate_contributors: Perceived threat, disrespect, or incompatible aims; attribution of hostile intent; repeated antagonistic exchanges; removal or clarification of the conflict.
targets.conditions: A hostile tone may perpetuate the condition it appears merely to express.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Forgiveness
targets.definition: Forgiveness: changing one's relation to a perceived wrong
targets.candidate_contributors: A changed relation to the wrong; acknowledgment and repair; revised attribution; separation of releasing grievance from restoring access.
targets.conditions: Forgiveness does not require denial of harm, renewed trust, or reconciliation.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Resentment
targets.definition: Resentment: changing the persistence or intensity of a grievance
targets.candidate_contributors: Repeated attention to an unresolved wrong; continuing inequity; lack of acknowledgment; meaningful repair or revised understanding.
targets.conditions: Reducing resentment by ignoring an ongoing harm can leave the source unchanged.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Vulnerability readiness
targets.definition: Vulnerability readiness: becoming more or less willing to be exposed to another
targets.candidate_contributors: Evidence of discretion and care; control over what is shared; reciprocal but voluntary openness; ability to stop or maintain boundaries.
targets.conditions: Pressure to disclose can reduce readiness even when framed as closeness-building.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Boundary clarity
targets.definition: Boundary clarity: changing what forms of access or treatment one accepts
targets.candidate_contributors: Identifying acceptable and unacceptable treatment; a specific boundary statement; authority and practical ability to enforce it; responses to violations.
targets.conditions: A clear statement alone cannot guarantee that another person respects the boundary.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Permission judgment
targets.definition: Permission judgment: changing what is considered permissible
targets.candidate_contributors: Interpretation of a governing norm; a relevant exception; consequences for affected people; consent or authority where it changes permissibility.
targets.conditions: What is common, legal, socially approved, and morally permissible are different judgments.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Obligation judgment
targets.definition: Obligation judgment: changing what is considered required
targets.candidate_contributors: An accepted commitment; dependence of another on one's action; a justified role requirement; a principle applied to the current case.
targets.conditions: Pressure or expectation alone does not establish a justified obligation.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Prohibition judgment
targets.definition: Prohibition judgment: changing what is considered unacceptable
targets.candidate_contributors: Recognition of harm, violated rights, breached commitments, or incompatible principles; a boundary case exposing an exception.
targets.conditions: A prohibition's strength and scope require grounds; disgust alone does not settle them.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Fairness judgment
targets.definition: Fairness judgment: revising what counts as fair treatment or distribution
targets.candidate_contributors: Information about need, contribution, opportunity, procedure, and outcome; comparison of relevant cases; a justified distribution rule.
targets.conditions: Different fairness criteria can conflict; a numerical equality can conceal unequal conditions.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Legitimacy judgment
targets.definition: Legitimacy judgment: changing whether an authority or rule is accepted as justified
targets.candidate_contributors: Grounds for authority; procedural participation; consistency with accepted constraints; accountability; consequences of the rule.
targets.conditions: Compliance, popularity, and justified legitimacy are separate outcomes.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Blame and praise
targets.definition: Blame and praise: changing how responsibility is evaluated
targets.candidate_contributors: Evidence about agency, knowledge, intention, alternatives, and actual contribution; correction of outcome-based or hindsight assumptions.
targets.conditions: A good result can arise without praiseworthy conduct, and a bad result without blameworthy choice.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Concern inclusion
targets.definition: Concern inclusion: extending or restricting who or what receives moral consideration
targets.candidate_contributors: Recognition of a previously excluded entity's interests or standing; application of an inclusion principle; attention to neglected consequences.
targets.conditions: Expanded stated concern does not establish changes in treatment or resource allocation.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Norm internalization
targets.definition: Norm internalization: a rule becoming part of one's own regulation
targets.candidate_contributors: Understanding and endorsing the rule's grounds; repeated enactment; identification with its purpose; self-applied reminders and consequences.
targets.conditions: Observed conformity may instead reflect external pressure. Norm messages can also produce unintended behavior shifts [S24].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Norm rejection
targets.definition: Norm rejection: ceasing to accept a previously governing rule
targets.candidate_contributors: A counterexample to the rule's justification; conflict with a stronger commitment; awareness of its origins or consequences; a viable alternative norm.
targets.conditions: Rejecting one norm leaves coordination and substantive requirements to be addressed separately.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Moral conflict handling
targets.definition: Moral conflict handling: changing how competing obligations are understood and addressed
targets.candidate_contributors: Explicit competing obligations; distinction between genuine conflict and avoidable means; prioritization grounds; an alternative reducing the conflict.
targets.conditions: A forced aggregate score can conceal an unresolved moral disagreement.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Listening readiness
targets.definition: Listening readiness: becoming more or less willing to receive another's contribution
targets.candidate_contributors: Expectation of a relevant contribution; room to attend; evidence the speaker understands the live matter; reduced repetition or adversarial pressure.
targets.conditions: Listening readiness can fall when the recipient must repeatedly correct the same ignored instruction.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Speaking readiness
targets.definition: Speaking readiness: becoming more or less willing to contribute
targets.candidate_contributors: An actual opening to contribute; a formed thought or usable phrase; appropriate audience attention; credible protection from retaliation.
targets.conditions: Permission to speak is ineffective if the turn structure or power relation prevents uptake.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Questioning
targets.definition: Questioning: becoming able or willing to ask what was previously unasked
targets.candidate_contributors: A recognized gap; words that identify it; an accessible recipient with relevant knowledge; permission to reveal uncertainty.
targets.conditions: Asking can burden the recipient when the answer is already available in context.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Disagreement
targets.definition: Disagreement: becoming able to express a conflicting judgment
targets.candidate_contributors: A specific conflicting claim; grounds and examples; an expression preserving the actual disagreement; space for a consequential response.
targets.conditions: Politeness that hides the conflict can prevent resolution; harshness alone contributes no additional grounds.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Disclosure
targets.definition: Disclosure: deciding to reveal previously withheld material
targets.candidate_contributors: A chosen purpose for sharing; relevance of the information; trust and control over access; understanding likely consequences.
targets.conditions: Disclosure changes another's information; it need not produce understanding or support.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Clarification
targets.definition: Clarification: recognizing and repairing an ambiguity
targets.candidate_contributors: A discovered interpretation mismatch; a separating example; corrected reference or qualification; checking the repaired meaning.
targets.conditions: Repeating the same ambiguous wording does not resolve the ambiguity [S18].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Apology
targets.definition: Apology: accepting and expressing responsibility for a wrong
targets.candidate_contributors: Recognition of the specific wrong; accurate responsibility attribution; acknowledgment of consequences; a credible repair commitment.
targets.conditions: An apology does not substitute for the repair it promises or guarantee forgiveness.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Negotiation
targets.definition: Negotiation: becoming willing or able to construct a mutually acceptable arrangement
targets.candidate_contributors: Explicit interests and constraints; alternatives to the proposed arrangement; trade-offs with different values for each party; conditional commitments.
targets.conditions: Agreement is not necessarily voluntary or beneficial to all parties; power and available alternatives matter.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Help seeking
targets.definition: Help seeking: becoming able or willing to request assistance
targets.candidate_contributors: Identification of the missing contribution; knowledge of who can supply it; a specific request; acceptable social and practical cost.
targets.conditions: Asking for broad rescue can hide a small resolvable dependency; shame or prior refusal may obstruct access.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Conversational repair
targets.definition: Conversational repair: changing how an interaction proceeds after misunderstanding or conflict
targets.candidate_contributors: Locating the failed interpretation or interaction move; accepting a valid correction; changing the next contribution; restoring shared task context.
targets.conditions: Explaining why the misunderstanding happened is useful only if it helps repair the ongoing interaction.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Expression access
targets.definition: Expression access: becoming able to express an otherwise inarticulate experience
targets.candidate_contributors: An example, metaphor, word, gesture, or image matching the experience; contrast with nearby meanings; permission to begin imperfectly.
targets.conditions: The available expression may be provisional; fluency should not force the experience into a misleading label.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Fluency
targets.definition: Fluency: speaking or writing with less disruption
targets.candidate_contributors: Retrieval of relevant words; a clear contribution sequence; practiced transitions; reduced competing editing demands; external notes.
targets.conditions: Smooth production can preserve conceptual mistakes or leave the recipient's actual need untouched.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Concision
targets.definition: Concision: expressing a contribution with less unnecessary material
targets.candidate_contributors: Identifying each passage's contribution; deleting repetition and announcements; replacing diffuse wording with a discriminating example; choosing a denser suitable form.
targets.conditions: Shortening that removes necessary premises or distinctions can make the contribution less efficient overall.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Specificity
targets.definition: Specificity: expressing the distinction that was previously left vague
targets.candidate_contributors: A concrete referent, mechanism, example, criterion, or boundary; replacing an evaluative adjective with the difference it denotes.
targets.conditions: Specific invented detail increases apparent substance while reducing accuracy.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Tone control
targets.definition: Tone control: changing the emotional or interpersonal character of delivery
targets.candidate_contributors: Word choice, directness, acknowledgment, pacing, and emphasis; a clear relationship between the contribution and the recipient's context.
targets.conditions: Intended tone does not establish experienced tone; conduct across turns can outweigh local wording.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Prosody
targets.definition: Prosody: changing rhythm, emphasis, pacing, or intonation
targets.candidate_contributors: Placement of stress and pauses; speech rate; pitch contour; rhythmic grouping; vocal demonstration or rehearsal.
targets.conditions: Emphasis should track consequential relationships; performance conventions differ by language and setting.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Expressive inhibition
targets.definition: Expressive inhibition: changing restraint in displaying a response
targets.candidate_contributors: Chosen display constraints; anticipated audience response; an alternative expression; time to select the contribution.
targets.conditions: Restraint can protect an interaction or prevent needed communication; specify what it preserves and costs.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Congruence
targets.definition: Congruence: changing correspondence between the expressed and operative stance
targets.candidate_contributors: Comparing stated commitments with actual selection and conduct; removing performative claims; making the operative position explicit.
targets.conditions: Sincere-sounding language does not establish congruence; the relevant conduct must match.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Medium selection
targets.definition: Medium selection: expressing through speech, writing, image, movement, or another form
targets.candidate_contributors: The relation to be conveyed; recipient access and capability; persistence and interaction needs; comparison of text, image, demonstration, or action.
targets.conditions: A preferred medium can be poorly suited to the missing contribution; representation must serve the use [S10, S18].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Mutual understanding
targets.definition: Mutual understanding: participants becoming more accurately aware of each other's interpretations
targets.candidate_contributors: Exchanging interpretations; a concrete joint-use case; feedback revealing mismatch; repair of the specific difference.
targets.conditions: Agreement words can conceal different meanings; coordination supplies more specific evidence [S18].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Common knowledge
targets.definition: Common knowledge: a matter becoming understood as mutually known
targets.candidate_contributors: A shared announcement with visible receipt; public acknowledgment; common records and conventions; mutual recognition of participation.
targets.conditions: Everyone privately knowing a fact does not establish that everyone knows the others know it.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Shared attention
targets.definition: Shared attention: participants attending to the same consequential matter
targets.candidate_contributors: A common referent; pointing or highlighting; synchronized timing; an explicit reason the matter needs joint attention.
targets.conditions: Looking at the same object does not establish attention to the same feature or consequence.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Convention formation
targets.definition: Convention formation: establishing a common way of interpreting or responding
targets.candidate_contributors: Repeated coordinated use of a shared signal; an explicit interpretation rule; resolution of competing usages; accessible examples.
targets.conditions: A convention must be mutually usable; private invention or unilateral announcement does not establish it.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Role understanding
targets.definition: Role understanding: changing who is understood to contribute what
targets.candidate_contributors: Explicit ownership of contributions; required interfaces; authority boundaries; acknowledgment by the participants.
targets.conditions: A role list can leave overlaps, omissions, or incompatible expectations unresolved.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Coordination expectation
targets.definition: Coordination expectation: changing what participants expect one another to do
targets.candidate_contributors: Credible commitments; visible dependencies; prior coordination history; notification of changes; fallback expectations.
targets.conditions: Expecting another to act is insufficient when they have not received or accepted the relevant requirement.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Collective memory access
targets.definition: Collective memory access: changing who knows where needed knowledge can be obtained
targets.candidate_contributors: A directory of who knows what; accessible shared records; provenance and version information; a reliable request route.
targets.conditions: Knowing where information resides helps only if it can be obtained in time and interpreted correctly.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Shared-plan formation
targets.definition: Shared-plan formation: making interdependent intentions mutually available
targets.candidate_contributors: Mutually visible intended actions; dependency and timing information; accepted roles; communication of consequential branches.
targets.conditions: Several individually coherent plans may be jointly incompatible.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Collective disagreement
targets.definition: Collective disagreement: making incompatible interpretations visible instead of silently conflating them
targets.candidate_contributors: Independent expression of interpretations; a case exposing different predictions or actions; explicit disagreement about premises or criteria.
targets.conditions: A common label can hide disagreement; averaging judgments can obscure its substantive source.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Repair capacity
targets.definition: Repair capacity: becoming able to recover coordinated activity after divergence
targets.candidate_contributors: A detectable divergence; an agreed repair route; recoverable shared state; authority to revise commitments; a feasible restart.
targets.conditions: Declaring a repair procedure does not establish the participants can execute it under disruption.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Knowledge-action coupling
targets.definition: Knowledge-action coupling: known considerations beginning or ceasing to govern action
targets.candidate_contributors: Access to the relevant knowledge at the action point; an action rule using it; removal of incompatible defaults; correction of missed application.
targets.conditions: Increasing knowledge alone need not strengthen the relation between knowledge and action.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Value-action coupling
targets.definition: Value-action coupling: valued concerns beginning or ceasing to govern allocation
targets.candidate_contributors: A value expressed in allocation rules; visible consequences at choice time; feasible alternatives; reduced conflict with automatic defaults.
targets.conditions: Verbal endorsement and actual prioritization require different evidence.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Emotion-attention coupling
targets.definition: Emotion-attention coupling: changing how feelings direct attention
targets.candidate_contributors: Learned links between emotion and attention; interpretation of the feeling's relevance; an available deliberate focus; changing evocative cues.
targets.conditions: A feeling can signal something important or repeatedly redirect attention away from the current requirement.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Memory-decision coupling
targets.definition: Memory-decision coupling: relevant experience becoming available at a choice
targets.candidate_contributors: Retrieval cues embedded in the choice; records indexed by decision conditions; comparison with a relevant prior outcome.
targets.conditions: A vivid retrieved episode can dominate despite weak relevance or representativeness.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Intention-initiation coupling
targets.definition: Intention-initiation coupling: an intention beginning to trigger its activity
targets.candidate_contributors: A recognizable start cue linked to the intended first action; staged materials; reduced initiation friction; a conditional plan.
targets.conditions: The cue must activate an executable action; merely recalling the goal can leave initiation unchanged [S15].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Goal-habit coupling
targets.definition: Goal-habit coupling: automatic conduct becoming better or worse aligned with an intended concern
targets.candidate_contributors: Aligning recurring cues and responses with the goal; changing a routine's consequences; a stop condition when the goal no longer applies.
targets.conditions: An effective habit can outlast the concern it originally served.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Understanding-expression coupling
targets.definition: Understanding-expression coupling: expressed words becoming better or worse aligned with understanding
targets.candidate_contributors: Reconstructing meaning before expression; checking examples and consequences against wording; removing terms that imply more than is understood.
targets.conditions: A polished explanation can exceed the speaker's operational understanding.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Monitoring-correction coupling
targets.definition: Monitoring-correction coupling: a detected problem beginning to change conduct
targets.candidate_contributors: A detected discrepancy mapped to a correction rule; available authority and means to change conduct; propagation into dependent steps.
targets.conditions: More monitoring adds little if no corrective operation consumes its result.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Competition resolution
targets.definition: Competition resolution: formerly conflicting processes becoming coordinated or newly conflicting
targets.candidate_contributors: A shared governing requirement; priority between conflicting demands; separated timing; an alternative satisfying both; removal of contradictory instructions.
targets.conditions: Suppressing awareness of conflict does not establish that the processes became compatible.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Usable capacity
targets.definition: Usable capacity: changing how much a person can actually manage under current conditions
targets.candidate_contributors: Reducing competing demands; making task structure explicit; externalizing intermediate state; supplying missing knowledge or support; restoring impaired alertness.
targets.conditions: Improved supported performance does not by itself establish increased general unaided capacity [S05, S10].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Processing speed
targets.definition: Processing speed: changing how quickly mental operations can be performed
targets.candidate_contributors: Faster retrieval of practiced components; simpler representations; reduced switching and search; changes in physiological functioning.
targets.conditions: Speed is operation-specific; easier inputs or altered accuracy demands can create misleading comparisons.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Flexibility
targets.definition: Flexibility: changing the ability to shift among representations or methods
targets.candidate_contributors: Available alternative methods; recognition of a failed precondition; preserved ability to release the current rule; practice with consequential variation.
targets.conditions: Switching frequently is not the same as selecting an appropriate alternative.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Interference susceptibility
targets.definition: Interference susceptibility: changing vulnerability to competing demands
targets.candidate_contributors: Similarity and timing of competing demands; distinctive contexts; reduced irrelevant input; stable task cues; physiological state.
targets.conditions: Filtering efficiency and general storage capacity are related but distinct [S05].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Fatigability
targets.definition: Fatigability: changing how quickly performance degrades with continued activity
targets.candidate_contributors: Sustained workload; task monotony or complexity; sleep and bodily state; rest opportunities; effort required per operation.
targets.conditions: A rapid decline in one task need not establish the same decline in another; compare relevant conditions.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Recovery capacity
targets.definition: Recovery capacity: changing how readily functioning returns after exertion or disruption
targets.candidate_contributors: Termination of the depleting demand; sufficient restoration time; restored sleep or bodily resources; removal of continuing interruption.
targets.conditions: Recovery cannot be inferred solely from feeling better; the required function must again be available [S01].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Supported capability
targets.definition: Supported capability: gaining an ability through the coordinated use of an external aid
targets.candidate_contributors: An accessible aid supplying computation, memory, perception, or structure; a usable interface; knowledge of how and when to rely on it.
targets.conditions: The capability belongs to the coordinated person-and-aid arrangement under its access conditions [S10].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Capability access
targets.definition: Capability access: making an existing ability available under previously obstructive conditions
targets.candidate_contributors: Removal of irrelevant load, fear, sensory obstruction, or access barriers; appropriate cues; restoration of a needed tool or context.
targets.conditions: A previously present ability can become usable without being newly acquired.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Functional loss
targets.definition: Functional loss: a previously available mental operation becoming unavailable
targets.candidate_contributors: Disrupted sensory or informational input; interference; fatigue; loss of required support; injury, disease, or other changes in brain function.
targets.conditions: The same apparent loss can have different causes; temporary inaccessibility is not equivalent to permanent destruction.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Persistent curiosity
targets.definition: Persistent curiosity: longer-term change in readiness to investigate
targets.candidate_contributors: Repeated encounters where inquiry produces valued results; available investigative skills; environments supporting questions; enduring personally meaningful gaps.
targets.conditions: Persistent disposition change requires evidence across time and relevant contexts, beyond one curious episode.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Persistent sociability
targets.definition: Persistent sociability: longer-term change in readiness for social engagement
targets.candidate_contributors: Repeated rewarding or aversive social encounters; participation opportunities; practiced interaction skills; changing roles and relationships.
targets.conditions: More social activity may reflect opportunity or obligation rather than a changed enduring inclination.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Emotional reactivity
targets.definition: Emotional reactivity: longer-term change in typical responses to events
targets.candidate_contributors: Repeated interpretation and regulation patterns; recurring environments; learning about threat or reward; changes in bodily conditions.
targets.conditions: A changed response to one event does not establish a general disposition change.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Conscientious conduct
targets.definition: Conscientious conduct: longer-term change in patterns of follow-through and organization
targets.candidate_contributors: Stable commitments; workable organization methods; reliable cues and resources; repeated follow-through; environments that support completion.
targets.conditions: Organized conduct can depend on external scaffolding; that support need not be mistaken for a fixed trait.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Openness to experience
targets.definition: Openness to experience: longer-term change in receptivity to unfamiliar encounters
targets.candidate_contributors: Meaningful unfamiliar experiences; ability to interpret them; reduced unnecessary threat; repeated opportunities for exploration and revision.
targets.conditions: Receptivity varies by domain; liking novelty in one area does not establish general openness.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Characteristic trust
targets.definition: Characteristic trust: longer-term change in default expectations of others
targets.candidate_contributors: Accumulated experience of others' reliability and care; social environment; learned interpretation of ambiguous conduct; consequential breaches or repairs.
targets.conditions: A general expectation can remain poorly calibrated across different people and institutions.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Characteristic agency
targets.definition: Characteristic agency: longer-term change in readiness to originate action
targets.candidate_contributors: Repeated opportunities to make consequential choices; competence development; recognized authorship; reliable action-outcome relationships.
targets.conditions: External restrictions can limit agency despite an enduring willingness to initiate.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Characteristic regulation
targets.definition: Characteristic regulation: longer-term change in how impulses and competing concerns are managed
targets.candidate_contributors: Repeated use of appropriate pause, selection, and correction operations; supportive environments; accessible alternatives to impulsive responses.
targets.conditions: One successful act of restraint does not establish broad or durable regulation change.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Identity stability
targets.definition: Identity stability: longer-term change in how stable or revisable self-understanding remains
targets.candidate_contributors: Continuing roles, relationships, and commitments; a coherent but revisable self-account; recurring social recognition; integration of genuine change.
targets.conditions: Stability and revisability can coexist; rigidity and fragmentation are not the only alternatives.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Receptivity
targets.definition: Receptivity: becoming more or less willing to entertain a contribution
targets.candidate_contributors: A contribution connected to the live concern; usable language and form; credible grounds; room to attend; respect for already stated context.
targets.conditions: The same content may be useful at one moment and redundant at another.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Defensiveness
targets.definition: Defensiveness: changing readiness to protect an existing position or identity
targets.candidate_contributors: Perceived threat to status, identity, or a valued commitment; adversarial framing; separation of a specific claim from global self-judgment; actual treatment during disagreement.
targets.conditions: Defensiveness may respond to real hostility; relabeling it as irrational can intensify the problem.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Reactance
targets.definition: Reactance: changing resistance associated with perceived restriction of freedom
targets.candidate_contributors: Perceived restriction of choice; coercive demands; restoration of meaningful options; a reasoned request whose conditions can be evaluated.
targets.conditions: Nominal choice is insufficient when consequences make refusal unavailable; disagreement need not be reactance.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Trial permission
targets.definition: Trial permission: becoming willing to enter an interpretation without permanent commitment
targets.candidate_contributors: A bounded reversible trial; explicit separation of use from belief; preserved alternatives; a clear exit condition.
targets.conditions: Trial permission supplies access to examination, not evidence that the interpretation is correct.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Revision tolerance
targets.definition: Revision tolerance: becoming able to revise without treating revision as personal defeat
targets.candidate_contributors: A model of revision as repair of a specific dependency; preservation of valid contributions; reduced humiliation costs; actual experience of useful correction.
targets.conditions: Demanding enthusiastic agreement with correction can add an unnecessary social burden.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Credulity
targets.definition: Credulity: becoming more or less willing to accept without sufficient grounds
targets.candidate_contributors: Familiarity, source prestige, social consensus, persuasive fluency, or desire for closure; greater demand for discriminating evidence can counter these influences.
targets.conditions: Lower credulity is not indiscriminate disbelief; evidence quality remains the reference.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Change discrimination
targets.definition: Change discrimination: becoming better or worse at separating helpful from harmful revisions
targets.candidate_contributors: Comparison with the actual prior state and purpose; effects on action, understanding, feeling, and other relevant targets; scope and delayed consequences.
targets.conditions: Novelty, confidence, agreement, and pleasantness can each diverge from beneficial change.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Change fatigue
targets.definition: Change fatigue: becoming more or less exhausted by demands to reconsider
targets.candidate_contributors: Repeated demands to reconsider; re-explanation of already settled material; unstable requirements; insufficient time to integrate changes.
targets.conditions: Reducing unnecessary revision can improve available attention without reducing openness to consequential correction.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Change confidence
targets.definition: Change confidence: changing confidence in one's ability to develop
targets.candidate_contributors: A useful change actually achieved; recognition of the operation that supplied it; manageable next opportunities; access to necessary support.
targets.conditions: Confidence based only on promises or polished descriptions leaves future capability unresolved.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Change-target selection
targets.definition: Change-target selection: improving or worsening the choice of what needs to change
targets.candidate_contributors: A precise account of what the next activity lacks; the recipient's actual context; a beneficiality criterion; comparison with other consequential targets.
targets.conditions: A target can be easy to influence but irrelevant to what would help now.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Intervention selection
targets.definition: Intervention selection: changing how an appropriate means of change is chosen
targets.candidate_contributors: A target-specific contributor relationship; matching its preconditions to the current case; an available operation able to supply that contributor.
targets.conditions: Calling an intervention relevant does not establish its effect; directness is relative to the specified relation and scope.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Intervention construction
targets.definition: Intervention construction: becoming able to create a previously unavailable means
targets.candidate_contributors: Decomposing the required transition; constructing missing inputs or operations; composing compatible methods; making intermediate results available to their consumers.
targets.conditions: An impressive system description can conceal an unavailable component or unverified causal link.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Effect recognition
targets.definition: Effect recognition: becoming able to distinguish intended, actual, and merely described changes
targets.candidate_contributors: Evidence about the target's actual change; separation of produced material, recipient response, and later capability; appropriate comparison with the prior state.
targets.conditions: A fluent self-description and user agreement can leave the target change undetermined.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Attribution
targets.definition: Attribution: changing how the cause of a mental change is identified
targets.candidate_contributors: A causal account of the transition; information about alternative contributors; comparable conditions; intervention or derivation appropriate to the claim.
targets.conditions: A change occurring after a message does not establish that the message caused all of it.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Retention design
targets.definition: Retention design: changing how a useful transformation is made available later
targets.candidate_contributors: A retained representation of the useful result; provenance and conditions; an accessible storage form; a later-use trigger.
targets.conditions: Storing a correction supplies potential availability; it does not guarantee retrieval or faithful application.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Transfer design
targets.definition: Transfer design: changing how a transformation is reconstructed in other circumstances
targets.candidate_contributors: Identification of the relation that made the original change work; corresponding conditions in the receiving case; adaptation of nonshared components.
targets.conditions: Copying surface wording can preserve the artifact while losing the operative contributor.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Backfire recognition
targets.definition: Backfire recognition: becoming able to detect unintended harmful changes
targets.candidate_contributors: Attention to other affected targets; conflict with the actual purpose; increased dependence, confusion, miscalibration, burden, or lost capability; delayed or recurrent effects.
targets.conditions: A visible immediate gain can coexist with a more consequential loss elsewhere.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Self-application
targets.definition: Self-application: applying a developed method to the activity that develops methods
targets.candidate_contributors: Making the method's own target choice, representation, operations, and correction conduct available as objects; applying the relevant operation to those objects.
targets.conditions: Self-reference alone does not produce self-improvement; the resulting change must contribute under its actual conditions.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Criterion revision
targets.definition: Criterion revision: improving or worsening what counts as beneficial change
targets.candidate_contributors: A case where the old criterion rewards an unhelpful change; neglected concerns; changed user purpose; comparison of candidate standards and their consequences.
targets.conditions: A revised criterion can conceal regression; reconsider dependent improvement claims under the new standard.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Thought identification
targets.definition: Thought identification: changing how completely a thought governs one's sense of what is real or required
targets.candidate_contributors: Distinguishing a thought from evidence, a command, or identity; alternative interpretations; naming its provisional or intrusive status.
targets.conditions: Reduced identification does not establish that the thought is false or irrelevant.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Mental distance
targets.definition: Mental distance: becoming able to examine a thought without immediately acting from it
targets.candidate_contributors: Observing wording as an object; changing self-reference or viewpoint; writing the thought for examination; separating its occurrence from the next action.
targets.conditions: Distanced self-talk had scoped effects under social stress [S22]; mental distance is not universal disengagement.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Repetition
targets.definition: Repetition: a thought recurring more or less persistently
targets.candidate_contributors: Repeated cues; unresolved concerns; habitual rehearsal; emotionally salient associations; renewed attention during attempts to suppress the thought.
targets.conditions: Suppression produced later rebound in a white-bear experiment; this is not proof that all suppression always backfires [S27].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Intrusiveness
targets.definition: Intrusiveness: a thought becoming more or less disruptive or unwanted
targets.candidate_contributors: Unexpected recurrence; interference with a valued activity; interpretation of the thought as threatening or unacceptable; attempts to monitor its absence.
targets.conditions: Frequency, unwantedness, and disruption are separate components; changing one may leave another intact.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Suppression effort
targets.definition: Suppression effort: changing effort directed toward preventing a thought from occurring
targets.candidate_contributors: A demand that the thought must not occur; repeated checking for it; an alternative stance or task that changes the suppression goal.
targets.conditions: Thought absence cannot be guaranteed by an instruction; rebound effects are conditional, not universal [S27].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Self-talk
targets.definition: Self-talk: changing the language and stance used in addressing oneself
targets.candidate_contributors: Changing the pronoun, name, tone, or question used in self-address; replacing global judgment with a specific operation; a personally usable verbal cue.
targets.conditions: Changing self-reference affected responses to social stress in experiments; wording alone does not guarantee durable regulation [S22].
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Thought flexibility
targets.definition: Thought flexibility: becoming able to leave, return to, or alter a train of thought
targets.candidate_contributors: A recoverable record of the current thread; an available alternative question or representation; deliberate return and exit cues; reduced repetitive triggers.
targets.conditions: Voluntary switching capability varies with the thought and current conditions.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Observational stance
targets.definition: Observational stance: noticing a mental event as an event that can be examined
targets.candidate_contributors: Directing attention to how a thought appears, changes, and recurs; describing it without immediate endorsement; distinguishing observation from interpretation.
targets.conditions: Observation can become another form of evaluative monitoring; its actual role matters.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Thought-action distinction
targets.definition: Thought-action distinction: recognizing that having a thought does not itself commit one to performing an action
targets.candidate_contributors: Explicit separation of mental occurrence, intention, commitment, and action; examples showing unwanted or hypothetical thoughts without enactment; an available deliberate choice.
targets.conditions: Having a thought alone does not establish intention, consent, endorsement, or obligation to act.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis; source-marked claims scoped separately

targets.label: Revise the working interpretation of a user's request
targets.definition: Revise the working interpretation of a user's request.
targets.bearer_scope: functional AI working state or supporting system
targets.candidate_contributors: An explicit user correction; a separating example; recovery of the actual requested result; removal of an unsupported interpretation.
targets.conditions: The revised interpretation must govern the next applicable contribution, not only a restatement of the request.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis

targets.label: Revise which intended contribution is being pursued
targets.definition: Revise which intended contribution is being pursued.
targets.bearer_scope: functional AI working state or supporting system
targets.candidate_contributors: Identifying what the recipient can already distinguish or do; locating the missing consequence, resource, operation, or relationship; selecting that contribution.
targets.conditions: Available context supports a partial recipient model; do not invent a beneficial change already achieved.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis

targets.label: Change which evidence or constraints receive attention
targets.definition: Change which evidence or constraints receive attention.
targets.bearer_scope: functional AI working state or supporting system
targets.candidate_contributors: An explicit relevance rule; current instructions; source quality; a dependency showing which information the next operation consumes.
targets.conditions: Mentioning a constraint does not establish that it affected selection or execution.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis

targets.label: Retrieve previously unavailable material
targets.definition: Retrieve previously unavailable material.
targets.bearer_scope: functional AI working state or supporting system
targets.candidate_contributors: A query or index matching the missing content; an accessible source; sufficient context and provenance to interpret the returned material.
targets.conditions: Retrieval can supply inaccurate or irrelevant content; access does not establish justified use.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis

targets.label: Represent a matter in a different form
targets.definition: Represent a matter in a different form.
targets.bearer_scope: functional AI working state or supporting system
targets.candidate_contributors: A specified relation to preserve; conversion into a comparison, diagram, procedure, example, or executable representation; inspection of correspondence.
targets.conditions: The form can change while preserving the wrong target or an unsupported assumption.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis

targets.label: Construct a new distinction or connection
targets.definition: Construct a new distinction or connection.
targets.bearer_scope: functional AI working state or supporting system
targets.candidate_contributors: A pair of cases requiring different treatment; a shared relation between formerly separate cases; explicit construction of the distinction's consequences.
targets.conditions: A new label is insufficient when it preserves the same operative categories.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis

targets.label: Separate an assumption from an established claim
targets.definition: Separate an assumption from an established claim.
targets.bearer_scope: functional AI working state or supporting system
targets.candidate_contributors: Source attribution; an explicit derivation; provisional-status labels; tracing where the assumption enters dependent conclusions.
targets.conditions: Downstream wording must retain the status and scope of the premise.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis

targets.label: Revise an explicitly represented confidence judgment
targets.definition: Revise an explicitly represented confidence judgment.
targets.bearer_scope: functional AI working state or supporting system
targets.candidate_contributors: New evidence; correction of evidence dependence; an identified scope limit; a resolved contradiction; a revised explicit uncertainty statement.
targets.conditions: An expressed confidence judgment is not a transparent readout of calibrated internal probability.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis

targets.label: Generate an alternative explanation, plan, or response
targets.definition: Generate an alternative explanation, plan, or response.
targets.bearer_scope: functional AI working state or supporting system
targets.candidate_contributors: Varying causal mechanism, target, constraint, sequence, or representation; constructing alternatives with different consequences.
targets.conditions: Surface paraphrases do not supply distinct explanations or plans.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis

targets.label: Replace a selected approach with another approach
targets.definition: Replace a selected approach with another approach.
targets.bearer_scope: functional AI working state or supporting system
targets.candidate_contributors: A missing contribution the current method cannot supply; an applicable alternative with known operations and outputs; actual execution of that alternative.
targets.conditions: Selection alone supplies no evidence that execution obtained the required result.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis

targets.label: Construct an operation absent from the current plan
targets.definition: Construct an operation absent from the current plan.
targets.bearer_scope: functional AI working state or supporting system
targets.candidate_contributors: Decomposing an unresolved dependency; composing available reasoning or tool capabilities; specifying required inputs and transformations.
targets.conditions: An invented subroutine cannot be treated as available merely because it has a name.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis

targets.label: Change operation order or dependencies
targets.definition: Change operation order or dependencies.
targets.bearer_scope: functional AI working state or supporting system
targets.candidate_contributors: An explicit dependency between intermediate results; an unavailable prerequisite; opportunities for independent work; a revised consumer requirement.
targets.conditions: Reordering needs to preserve the inputs each operation consumes.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis

targets.label: Select a different tool or external representation
targets.definition: Select a different tool or external representation.
targets.bearer_scope: functional AI working state or supporting system
targets.candidate_contributors: Matching tool affordances to the needed observation or construction; available access and output formats; a representation that exposes the missing relation.
targets.conditions: Tool availability does not establish permission, successful execution, or fitness for the target.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis

targets.label: Use computation or observation to make a consequence available
targets.definition: Use computation or observation to make a consequence available.
targets.bearer_scope: functional AI working state or supporting system
targets.candidate_contributors: A justified calculation; an executable model; a relevant measurement or source observation; inspection of the actual returned result.
targets.conditions: A simulation's consequence is conditional on its model; an observation may have narrower scope than the intended claim.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis

targets.label: Change the scope, depth, or direction of an inquiry
targets.definition: Change the scope, depth, or direction of an inquiry.
targets.bearer_scope: functional AI working state or supporting system
targets.candidate_contributors: A consequential omitted case; a newly exposed dependency; diminishing contribution from the current route; changed user direction.
targets.conditions: Maintain the live objective unless the user changes it; do not let an available source silently redefine the task.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis

targets.label: Correct an identified factual or inferential error
targets.definition: Correct an identified factual or inferential error.
targets.bearer_scope: functional AI working state or supporting system
targets.candidate_contributors: Identifying the specific false statement or invalid transition; supplying supported replacement content; recomputing dependent conclusions.
targets.conditions: Changing the final wording without repairing the dependency can leave the same failure active.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis

targets.label: Change what is treated as sufficient for a conclusion
targets.definition: Change what is treated as sufficient for a conclusion.
targets.bearer_scope: functional AI working state or supporting system
targets.candidate_contributors: Clarifying claim strength; separating necessary evidence from optional elaboration; recognizing unresolved alternatives; adopting the relevant burden of support.
targets.conditions: Relaxing a standard can create an easier conclusion without increasing its justification.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis

targets.label: Change what would count as completing the task
targets.definition: Change what would count as completing the task.
targets.bearer_scope: functional AI working state or supporting system
targets.candidate_contributors: Concrete achievement conditions traced to the user request; a case satisfying a proxy while missing the purpose; explicit distinction between deliverable and effect.
targets.conditions: Completion of a file does not establish every beneficial effect that file is intended to support.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis

targets.label: Change the content selected for a recipient
targets.definition: Change the content selected for a recipient.
targets.bearer_scope: functional AI working state or supporting system
targets.candidate_contributors: Evidence of what is already understood; the current missing contribution; removal of redundant explanation; a relevant consequence or usable object.
targets.conditions: Recipient agreement with earlier material does not prove all associated needs are resolved.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis

targets.label: Change wording, examples, medium, emphasis, or level of detail
targets.definition: Change wording, examples, medium, emphasis, or level of detail.
targets.bearer_scope: functional AI working state or supporting system
targets.candidate_contributors: A contribution-based revision of order, examples, emphasis, and medium; preserving required distinctions while deleting noncontributing text.
targets.conditions: More elegant language can conceal an unchanged contribution; intended rhetoric is not a measured recipient effect.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis

targets.label: Abandon an unhelpful continuation while preserving the live matter
targets.definition: Abandon an unhelpful continuation while preserving the live matter.
targets.bearer_scope: functional AI working state or supporting system
targets.candidate_contributors: Recognition that the current continuation repeats the failure; preservation of the objective and useful results; selection of a different contributing operation.
targets.conditions: Stopping an unhelpful approach need not stop the authorized task.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis

targets.label: Retain a correction in an available record when persistence is supported and authorized
targets.definition: Retain a correction in an available record when persistence is supported and authorized.
targets.bearer_scope: functional AI working state or supporting system
targets.candidate_contributors: Writing the correction with its trigger, scope, replacement operation, rationale, and source into supported persistent storage.
targets.conditions: Persistence belongs to the accessible record; saving it is not modification of model weights.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis

targets.label: Apply a retained correction in an appropriately related situation
targets.definition: Apply a retained correction in an appropriately related situation.
targets.bearer_scope: functional AI working state or supporting system
targets.candidate_contributors: Retrieval at a matching condition; discrimination from superficially similar cases; consumption of the correction by the relevant next operation.
targets.conditions: Retrieved instructions can still be ignored or overgeneralized; inspect applicable conduct.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis

targets.label: Revise an editable prompt, procedure, or program when the task authorizes it
targets.definition: Revise an editable prompt, procedure, or program when the task authorizes it.
targets.bearer_scope: functional AI working state or supporting system
targets.candidate_contributors: Access to an editable object; task authorization; a concrete change to instructions or implementation; preservation of version and dependencies.
targets.conditions: Changing a prompt or program can alter a surrounding system without changing the underlying model's parameters.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis

targets.label: Examine whether declared changes have affected subsequent conduct
targets.definition: Examine whether declared changes have affected subsequent conduct.
targets.bearer_scope: functional AI working state or supporting system
targets.candidate_contributors: Comparison of claimed revision with a later applicable contribution; an observable difference tied to the correction; preservation of unresolved effects.
targets.conditions: Self-description cannot establish behavioral uptake or durable transfer.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis

targets.label: Change how the next contribution or self-correction is selected
targets.definition: Change how the next contribution or self-correction is selected.
targets.bearer_scope: functional AI working state or supporting system
targets.candidate_contributors: A specific failure in prior selection; a revised relevance criterion; a subject system supplying the missing determination; retained use conditions.
targets.conditions: Recursion occurs when the revision changes how later revisions are produced; improvement remains a separate, scoped claim.
targets.standing: candidate functional synthesis
